#1874. Tottenham look set to deliver after so many disappointments but Roberto De Zerbi's side need a nasty streak if they are to build on their momentum ahead of a daunting festive period, writes RIATH AL-SAMARRAI

By RIATH AL-SAMARRAI, CHIEF SPORTS FEATURE WRITER

Published: 06:52 EDT, 1 November 2026 | Updated: 06:31 EDT, 2 November 2026

It was late on Saturday evening when Roberto De Zerbi relayed a few of the comments he had shared with Tottenham’s players at half-time in their 2-0 win over Crystal Palace. One of those remarks was indicative of how quickly things can change.

In the knowledge that his side were 45 minutes away from a rare spot in the upper portion of the table, he reminded them: ‘We can't forget where we have been two weeks ago. Two weeks ago, before the Coventry game, we were last in the table and we can't forget.’

With Tottenham, it is always prudent to know calamity is never too far away, but for the first time in two years, there is a gathering excitement at the club - in the crowd and the dressing room.

The win over Palace was assisted hugely by Jean-Philippe Mateta’s red card after 13 minutes, but Spurs have an uncanny knack of slipping on the easier opportunities. Not this time – goals from Archie Gray and Jan Paul van Hecke punctuated a dominant performance and a third straight win. Three managers and 616 days had expired since the last such streak.

But Spurs appear to be on the march and a promising season is belatedly taking shape. To finally deliver after so many disappointments, there are certain areas where improvements must follow…

Roberto De Zerbi reminded his players of where they had come from during their 2-0 win over Crystal Palace

That was De Zerbi’s own assessment of his frontline after a familiar shortcoming against Palace may have been concealed by the win. It was not lost on him that both of Tottenham’s goals were scored by defenders, nor that they had 34 shots to Palace’s two. As ever, Spurs had abundant creativity in their side but lacked a clinical edge.

De Zerbi said: ‘If we want to follow perfection, we have to be more nasty, no? That is an individual thing, because if I'm number nine, number 10, I want to score. But I can't say nothing.’

He later clarified that comment to encompass the whole side, but it was clear that the onus falls most on Dominic Solanke and Omar Marmoush.

In fairness to the pair, Palace defended so deep after Mateta’s dismissal that they had no space to operate, but one goal apiece this season is a poor return. Solanke, in particular, needs to do a better job of reading the movements and intentions of those around him – too often on Saturday he appeared a thought or two behind Mathys Tel and Mohammed Kudus, who both impressed in the more generous spaces out wide.

De Zerbi wants his side to develop a 'nasty' streak - particularly his attackers

Marmoush is an interesting case for De Zerbi. His mobility and technical ability are clear but he is yet to reveal his best position. On Saturday he was used as a No 10, having already been switched between roles on the left and up front. This experiment drew muted results.

It might be the case that a sustained run in one spot would be beneficial, but for now there appears to be confusion over where to use him. There is also a nagging thought that his best striking potential comes in a two-striker system, as shown in his most prolific period at Frankfurt, but that is not the way De Zerbi plays.

A significant improvement for Tottenham has come in midfield and, specifically, the pairing between Matheus Fernandes and Sandro Tonali.

Acquired at great cost, there was limited patience around the delivery of their impact, but time was always necessary, because De Zerbi’s system is notoriously complicated. In recent weeks, Fernandes and Tonali have shown signs that the penny has dropped on what they have to do.

This has been especially relevant in the instance of Tonali, who is very much the tempo-setter of the side on the ball and off it. On Saturday, he was excellent, or worth ‘double’ in the words of De Zerbi. There were times earlier in the season when he appeared disinterested, as if Tottenham was not the destination he had in mind, but his work rate was brilliant against Palace – he covered 12.3km, won all three of his tackles, and completed 93 per cent of his passes. He was all-action.

The same would be said for Fernandes, who covered 11.6km of ground and finessed a superb cross for Van Hecke’s goal. As a pair with Tonali, he was key to the pressing operation that limited Palace to a single counter-attack in the second half.

Mateus Fernandes (pictured) and Sandro Tonali have been huge boosts in the midfield

De Zerbi struck an interesting note after the game by alluding to the cohesiveness of his side and how it has changed on the pitch. Perhaps that relates to the recent team-bonding exercise in Marbella, but more likely they just needed time to understand the complexities of their manager’s demands.

‘I think even before the international break we were playing well,’ De Zerbi said. ‘We were playing maybe not 90 minutes, but many parts of the game we played very well. We didn't score. We conceded a stupid goal and then we lost energy. We lost spirit. We lost the right union between the players.

‘If we compare Tottenham before the international break and Tottenham after the international break, now we are playing as a team. Before the international break we were playing as many very good players, but not as a team.’

Archie Gray, for one, is getting to grips with the less familiar brief at right-back. The requirements to swap spots with Fernandes, overlap Kudus or hold the advanced position are mind-scrambling, but he has adapted well. His withdrawal at half-time against Palace was down to his first-half yellow card and doesn’t detract from a salient point – he can evidently be trusted to replace Pedro Porro, or at least give the latter scope for a breather.

Tottenham have an opportunity now. Their next four fixtures are Leeds, Ipswich, Sunderland and Fulham, with a nasty run waiting in December and early January.

If they can get something from Elland Road, the other three assignments present a rich opportunity for momentum before the tricky festive period.

One key area to improve in the short term will come against defensive sides who offer less space. That Spurs scored only twice from 80 per cent possession against Palace highlighted the issue.

De Zerbi said: ‘We are improving in the principle and the quality of play. Maybe we are not ready yet to play against such a low block but maybe in two or three months we will be.’

#1873. Piero Hincapie aims dig at Liverpool captain after Arsenal win at Anfield

Piero Hincapie has gone very niche with a dig at Liverpool captain Virgil van Dijk after the Gunners won at Anfield on Sunday.

Kai Havertz scored the only goal of an entertaining game on Merseyside as Mikel Arteta’s side climbed to the top of the Premier League table and the Reds remained fifth.

Despite there only being one goal and Liverpool not managing a shot on target, it was a great match with plenty of incident, including Alexis Mac Allister trying to get Noni Madueke sent off and being branded ’embarrassing’ by Jamie Carragher as a result.

There was clearly an edge to the match at times and that continued after the final whistle as Hincapie posted on Instagram.

It will not have been clear to all what he meant when he posted three pictures from the match with the caption: ‘I don’t forget…’

The third and final picture was a close up of the gold Premier League badge on the sleeve of Arsenal’s kit.

The gold logo is only worn by the defending champions in a Premier League season.

It was a response to Van Dijk doing the same in January after a goalless draw between Arsenal and Liverpool at the Emirates.

The Reds were defending champions at the time and the iconic centre-back was thought to be quietly reminding the north Londoners of that.

Use AI to go deeper into the stories you care about – powered by Metro and trusted publications.

Hincapie certainly saw it that way and has reminded the Liverpool great who are the champions right now.

It is still very early in the season but Arsenal look in a very strong position to lift the Premier League title again, moving three points clear of Manchester City thanks to an eighth win in nine league games.

The Gunners’ defence continues to be the source of their strength, with just five goals conceded in nine Premier League outings, three of which came in their one defeat to Brighton.

Liverpool were very competitive in the match, but could not produce a single shot on target, with Arteta crediting his entire team for the work they do defensively.

‘I didn’t know about that statistic but that’s incredible,’ he said of goalkeeper David Raya not having to make one save.

‘It didn’t feel like this to be fair on the pitch because there were very little margins sometimes when they had the opportunity to shoot and it’s a team that shoots a lot.

‘You have to be so good at blocking shots and preventing those spaces for them to get into there. Again, it’s a commitment of every single player in every action consistently to deliver those kind of stats and to do it against this team, it’s something remarkable I would say.’

#1872. Gary Neville speaks out on ‘remarkable’ Lisandro Martinez performances

Gary Neville says he would be ‘curled up in a ball’ if he was playing as badly as Lisandro Martinez is and certainly not pointing fingers at other people in interviews.

The Argentina international has been in dreadful form this season, much like most of his teammates, and was at fault again in the 2-0 defeat to Chelsea on Saturday.

The 28-year-old did little to prevent Morgan Rogers’ opener at Stamford Bridge and then picked up a second yellow card for a ridiculous challenge in the penalty area, which saw Cole Palmer convert from the spot.

It was a calamitous afternoon for Martinez after Manchester United had looked quite impressive in the first half, before falling apart after the break.

Neville had a damning assessment of the defender, saying he was not surprised at all to see him let his team down.

Martinez spoke out against the Manchester United hierarchy last month, criticising the lack of investment in the squad, but Neville thinks the Argentine is in no position to make such comments.

‘That’s what I expect from him, to be honest with you, that’s what I see,’ Neville told Sky Sports of Martinez’s performance at Chelsea.

‘I said the other week – and you’ve got to respect hat he is a World Cup winner – but every time I watch him for Manchester United he is at fault for a goal and he was at fault for two yesterday. The first goal is solely on him. I know the midfield could do better, but Harry Maguire has to go and watch that run and he has to come across.

‘If I was giving away the goals that he is giving away, I wouldn’t be doing interviews. And to be fair, I wouldn’t be speaking out, because I have to say, I would be curled up in a ball, if I was playing like that for Manchester United.

‘We all give goals away as defenders, but the quantity of goals he gives away is remarkable. And that defence is just nowhere near good enough and it falls apart every time it is put under big pressure and it did do in the second half.’

Martinez has been a mainstay in the heart of Michael Carrick’s defence, but will now serve a suspension and may not return to the side.

Carrick does have options, with the likes of Matthijs de Ligt and Ayden Heaven on the bench at Stamford Bridge, while Noussair Mazraoui is also an option, with Leny Yoro playing at right-back against Chelsea.

Former Liverpool and England midfielder Danny Murphy said Martinez should be out of contention after becoming a liability.

‘Lisandro Martinez has got a lot to answer to, because the first goal was mainly his fault. The sending-off is absolutely ridiculous,’ Murphy said on BBC Radio 5 Live.

‘Obviously, he is going to apologise in the dressing room, but his mindset is not right to play. You can’t rely on him. He is a liability.’

On whether he would pick the defender again, Murphy said: ‘No, I wouldn’t, only because he looks like he has already gone. His head isn’t right. He is not going to be there long term, that is evident.

‘Michael has got to make some big decisions. You can’t have a liability in your team. That petulance, that behaviour on the pitch is not acceptable.

‘He has been poor for a while and he has had injury problems. He is not the answer.’

#1871. Manchester United vs. Roma: Head-to-head record and past meetings before Champions League battle

By Seye Omidiora | 01 Nov 2026 23:39, Last updated: 03 Nov 2026 22:31

Manchester United and Roma have crossed paths nine times in major European competition, with every single encounter taking place in the 21st century across both the Champions League and the Europa League.

The Red Devils have historically dominated this fixture, coming out on top in six of those clashes, while suffering two defeats and sharing the spoils on one occasion.

The rivalry's inaugural chapter unfolded during the 2006-07 Champions League quarter-finals, where Roma initially gained the upper hand with a 2-1 first-leg victory at the Stadio Olimpico thanks to goals from Rodrigo Taddei and Mirko Vucinic.

However, Sir Alex Ferguson's men responded six days later by inflicting one of the most brutal scorelines in modern knockout history, tearing the Italians apart in an unforgettable 7-1 thrashing at Old Trafford, featuring braces from Cristiano Ronaldo and Michael Carrick.

Familiarity was taken to another level the following season in 2007-08, when the two European heavyweights locked horns four times in a single continental campaign.

Drawn together in Group F, Wayne Rooney settled a tense 1-0 win for United in Manchester before Gerard Pique and Mancini traded strikes in a 1-1 draw in Rome; the sides were then paired together again in the quarter-finals, where United secured a comfortable 3-0 aggregate triumph via a 2-0 away win and a 1-0 home success en route to lifting the trophy in Moscow.

The pair also met in the 2020-21 Europa League semi-finals, producing another goal-laden spectacle that tilted heavily toward the English giants.

Despite trailing 2-1 at the break in the first leg at Old Trafford, Ole Gunnar Solskjaer's side staged a devastating second-half blitz to secure a 6-2 win led by doubles from Edinson Cavani and Bruno Fernandes, which rendered Roma's spirited 3-2 victory in the Italian capital two weeks later mere consolation as United advanced 8-5 on aggregate.

Man United then recorded a 3-2 win over Roma in the Champions League league stage in November 2026, with the Red Devils coming from two goals behind to triumph.

Peter Schmeichel says he remains unconvinced that any team in the Premier League is capable of seriously challenging Arsenal following the side’s 1-0 victory over Liverpool.

#1866. Tottenham transfer news: Roberto De Zerbi ready to fight Man City for £12.5m 'favourite' of Mauricio Pochettino

By Lewis Nolan | 01 Nov 2026 23:45

Tottenham Hotspur will have to compete with Manchester City for Villarreal full-back Alexander Freeman, the latest report has claimed.

Spurs have started to improve considerably in the Premier League, collecting nine points from the last nine on offer.

Roberto De Zerbi's side most recently emerged as 2-0 winners against Crystal Palace on Saturday, but despite their strong form, there are concerns about the strength of the squad.

Pedro Porro did not start any of those three victories, and while the head coach has indicated that the defender is ready to make a return to the XI, the club must avoid aggravating his hamstring issue.

A new report from Football Insider claims that Spurs are interested in signing Villarreal right-back Freeman, though they may face competition from the likes of Manchester City for his signature.

Freeman enjoyed a strong showing with the United States of America at the 2026 World Cup under boss Mauricio Pochettino, making five appearances while scoring once and assisting once, though he is only price by Transfermarkt at £12.5m.

For Villarreal this campaign, the 22-year-old has played 14 times and started six games, and he has shown that he is not only a strong passer, but that he can also regularly win his duels.

It would be surprising if Tottenham looked to sign a starting right-back given Pedro Porro possesses immense quality.

However, the Spaniard has not started any of his side's last three games due to injury concerns, with Gray being forced to fill in.

Signing Freeman may allow Gray to be used in a more natural midfield role, while also giving Porro a suitable backup on the right.

Spurs fought against relegation in each of the last two seasons, and it is far too soon to suggest they have escaped the battle against the drop this term.

City are ordinarily in the hunt for every trophy available, but they could face severe sanctions after being found guilty of breaching Premier League spending rules.

Demotion has not been ruled out as a punishment, and prospective targets may be wary about joining before sanctions have been revealed, something that could give Spurs an edge in a transfer tussle.

#1864. First Anfield victory for 14 years was vindication for Mikel Arteta after Fleetwood humbling. His Arsenal look the finished article - Liverpool were authors of their own downfall, writes OLIVER HOLT

Published: 13:54 EDT, 1 November 2026 | Updated: 06:32 EDT, 2 November 2026

Five nights ago, 40 miles to the north of Anfield at a remote outpost of English football, Arsenal fell to one of the most humiliating reverses of their long and august history. In the teeth of a gale that blew in off the Irish Sea, they were knocked out of the League Cup by Fleetwood Town, a team 18th in League Two.

They left with their tails between their legs, their teenage prodigy Max Dowman sent off in a melee, their heart questioned, their quality debated, their discipline an issue. Mikel Arteta and his side knew that just a few days later, at the other end of the Fylde Coast and across the Ribble Estuary, they would have to swap running the gauntlet of the Cod Army for the challenge of facing down the roar of the Kop.

They did not shirk it. If Tuesday night was a humbling, their gritty 1-0 victory in an Anfield that was a cauldron once more felt like a significant triumph. It was a defensive masterclass from the champions, an exercise in indomitability. It was their first victory here since 2012 and it took them above Manchester City so that they sit, once more, at the top of the table. Liverpool could not summon a single shot on target.

‘It felt like the end of the world when we were knocked out at Fleetwood,’ Arteta said after this win. ‘You look so silly. I was thinking “How can I lift these players up?” You have to dig deep. This was a mission to win here and it is something that we have not done for 14 years for a variety of reasons. We knew we would have to navigate some difficult moments.’

If Arteta left Fleetwood answering questions about his management of Dowman, he finished this game by striding on to the pitch after the final whistle, pumping his fists in front of the Arsenal fans celebrating in the Anfield Road end, and beating his hand on his chest. This was a vindication for him and his team. Five nights is a long time in football.

He had talked about the harsh realities of this sport after Tuesday’s loss. He had reminded everyone that playing at this level was not like ‘Disneyland’. And this victory was not like Disneyland, either. It was less a theme park and more an assault course. It was rough and it was unforgiving and Arsenal were equal to it.

Liverpool, improving under the management of Andoni Iraola, had been talked up as title contenders ahead of this match on a dank evening on Merseyside where the streets around the ground were decorated with the toothless grimaces of rotting pumpkins on doorsteps. The home team showed exhilarating signs of their re-emergence as an attacking force.

They dominated much of the game, too, but they looked like an emerging team, a team that is still evolving. Arsenal, marshalled imperiously by Declan Rice, looked like the finished article. They created one outstanding chance and Kai Havertz converted it. That was all they needed.

Their defence stayed rock-solid, although there was some puzzlement that Liverpool were not awarded a penalty for Jurrien Timber’s blatant shirt-pull on Alexander Isak. After the interval, Liverpool rarely looked like drawing level.

Kai Havertz gave the Gunners a lead to defend after finishing off a well worked move early on

The German slotted home after Declan Rice fizzed a dangerous ball across the six-yard box

Winning at Anfield was vindication for Mikel Arteta after Arsenal's defeat by Fleetwood Town

The opening had been predictably frenetic. Neither team forged a chance but Trey Nyoni, who has forced his way into the first team with a series of excellent performances in midfield, could have been booked twice inside the first quarter of an hour.

The initial infringement was a nasty tackle on Martin Odegaard inside the first minute where he planted his studs in Odegaard’s ankle. The second was a spiteful tackle on Kai Havertz. Neither received a yellow card, which gave yet more pause for thought about the red card shown to Dowman at Fleetwood, and its aftermath.

Let’s get one thing straight – the criticism of Arteta for his ‘treatment’ of Dowman was absurd. It has come to something when a manager giving a player a hard stare is interpreted by some as a disproportionate response.

Nobody is necessarily hankering after a return to the days of Sir Alex Ferguson’s hairdrier or Joe Kinnear’s rants that broke records for expletives but if a boss is attracting censure because he looked at a player a bit funny, we are in big trouble.

Arteta is not there to indulge Dowman. He is there to coach him and to teach him and to help him grow up in the context of a Premier League football club. His actions in Fleetwood on Tuesday fulfilled his obligations in all of those criteria.

Arsenal survived the initial frenzy here and took the lead after 16 minutes. Liverpool were the authors of their own downfall. They gave the ball away from a goal kick, it was worked to Noni Madueke on the right, and when Madueke fed it to Declan Rice on the overlap, Rice crossed beautifully for Havertz, who touched it home at the back post.

Arsenal nearly returned the favour a minute later when they played themselves into trouble at the back. Bradley Barcola found himself through on David Raya but his first touch let him down and Rice moved across to clear the danger.

Alexis Mac Allister was left with his head in his hands after missing a glorious chance to score

Liverpool's 19-year-old talent Trey Nyoni started the match but was replaced in the second half

Liverpool recovered and began to dominate the game. Barcola’s pace began to cause Arsenal all sorts of problems down their right flank and Liverpool came close to an equaliser when Virgil van Dijk flicked on a corner and Alexander Isak was denied by the brave intervention of Raya.

Arsenal were still threatening on the counter. Christos Tzolis chipped a ball to the back post and, as Liverpool scrambled to clear it, Madueke turned it back across goal. The ball was intended for Havertz, who was unmarked in the middle, but Timber could not get out of the way of it and it bounced off him into touch.

The atmosphere was febrile. Liverpool had three appeals for penalties, first for Timber’s shirt pull on Isak, then for challenges on Alexis Mac Allister and Cody Gakpo, turned down in quick succession. Tempers began to flare on the benches.

The breathlessness of the match was relentless. Florian Wirtz drove a free kick against the face of the crossbar with Raya beaten and then, three minutes before the interval, Mac Allister ran on to a cross from Milos Kerkez and, with the goal at his mercy, directed his free header too high.

Liverpool laid siege to the Arsenal goal after the break but the openings just would not come. Isak blazed high over the bar from an angle, Wirtz had a shot on the turn blocked and then, just before the hour, Dominik Szoboszlai replaced Nyoni and, to more acclaim, Rio Ngumoha came on for Gakpo.

Still Liverpool could not prise Arsenal open. Arsenal began to grow in confidence and threat. The home team were grateful to Jeremy Jacquet for a clearance that prevented Odegaard turning Tzolis’s cross into an open goal, for Van Dijk’s brilliant interception to deny Havertz and, most of all, for a quite magnificent one-handed save from Alisson that diverted a Tzolis shot round the post. It will stand the test of time as one of the saves of the season.

Arsenal put in another excellent defensive display to frustrate and keep Liverpool at bay

Liverpool’s frustration boiled over. Mac Allister was booked for his part in an ugly fracas with Odegaard and Madueke. The stands became a mass of pointing fingers and shouts of protest and anger. Time-wasting and play-acting peppered the match. Liverpool felt the game slipping away in the angst.

Liverpool threw everything at it in the final minutes. Lewis Koumas flung himself at a bouncing ball but could not get enough power on his header, Ngumoha had a shot charged down, Barcola desperately searched for pockets of space but could not find them. There were six minutes of time added on but there was no way through. Arsenal’s defence would not yield.

#1862. GdS: Ten-point risk and high ambitions – three keys for Amorim in Milan-Inter

AC Milan are taking on their city rivals Inter this morning, and for Ruben Amorim, there is one key player in each department.

As highlighted by Gazzetta dello Sport this morning, Milan are entering the derby at a pretty clear disadvantage, currently seven points behind Inter in the standings. Ruben Amorim made it clear yesterday that the Scudetto remains the goal, but if the gap is increased to ten, it will be tough.

Read SempreMilan ad-free and get access to exclusive news. Click here for a free trial!

It’s true that Stefano Pioli, in February 2022, also risked going ten points behind until Olivier Giroud turned the game around. The problem is that his successor Goncalo Ramos hasn’t even scored a goal in the league since the end of August.

Furthermore, Cristian Chivu and his Inter have been in very good form lately and will be looking to end their seven-game run without a win in the fixture. It’s going to be a night with a lot of emotions, so let’s see how it will pan out on the pitch.

Mario Gila’s return is absolutely essential for Milan, but it will take more from them to regain solidity at the back. The Rossoneri have conceded four more goals than they did at this point last season, and six in their last two home games.

Switching from Max Allegri’s low block to Amorim’s more proactive style of play has clearly come with a cost. Yet, it’s not like the Rossoneri have been pressing like crazy so far, which is obvious when you compare them with Inter.

The Nerazzurri have a much higher centre of gravity (54.7-48.5 m), they steal more balls in the final third of the pitch (41-28), and they shoot more from offensive recoveries (13-7). Meanwhile, Milan are continuing to concentrate, play vertically and run quickly.

There is also another truth that needs to be highlighted: too many goals have been conceded due to individual errors. Amorim is well aware of this and it might have something to do with the decision to start Sankhoun Diawara on the left, with effectively four centre-backs in the back four.

In midfield, just like with Gila in defence, Amorim can count on another crucial return: Adrien Rabiot, the team’s top scorer along with Alphadjo Cisse (4 goals). For Milan, the midfielders are crucial with their goals.

The midfield is indeed the centre of Milan’s power, where the Ballon d’Or winner Luka Modric reigns supreme and where counterattacks that end up in goal are born. Amorim’s choices in this department weren’t easy.

The most tested on the eve of the match: a 4-3-3 with Musah and Rabiot on either side of Modric, and an attacking trident of Moreira-Ramos-Pulisic.

There were fewer doubts for Chivu who has a tested midfield and, in general, the most coherent team in the league. But that doesn’t mean they don’t have problems. Against Venezia, Inter suffered six dangerous transitions, against Roma there were seven.

In the middle of the pitch, due to the pressure of pressing or laziness in the return, there have often been gaps to exploit. It’s extremely dangerous to leave that space against galloping players like Diego Moreira, Christian Pulisic, and Rabiot.

The Frenchman, who already crippled Inter on the counterattack as a Juventus player (goal and assist for Kostic), could become a key factor in the derby.

Despite conceding one fewer goal than a year ago (10-11), as the pink newspaper continues, Inter appear to be more vulnerable at the back. The centre-backs have dipped in form and the conceded xG is much higher, which Milan will try to exploit.

Ramos is pushing hard to score his third league goal, which he desperately needs despite adding a lot to Milan’s game: 14 balls recovered (Thuram 4, Lautaro 5, Pio 8), 21 lay-offs (Thuram 7, Lautaro 8, Pio 13). All he has to do is find the net.

However, if the player that Milan fear the most is Thuram, then that player is Pulisic for Inter. He decided the penultimate derby, scored in the one that stopped the haemorrhage of six defeats, and also impressed in the Supercoppa Italiana.

He knows the art of hiding between the lines and striking from the attacking midfield, which Inter’s 3-5-2 often struggles to achieve. Perhaps he can celebrate his contract renewal by deciding yet another derby.

#1860. Manchester United predicted lineup vs. Roma: Micheal Carrick makes tough Lisandro Martinez decision

By Seye Omidiora | 01 Nov 2026 23:56

Manchester United head coach Michael Carrick faces a major defensive decision regarding Lisandro Martinez, but the centre-back is tipped to start on Tuesday night even though Matthijs de Ligt represents a strong alternative.

Indeed, Martinez is backed to feature from the off despite his recent scathing criticism of the club and a domestic suspension following his sending-off against Chelsea in the Premier League.

The Argentine should partner Harry Maguire in the heart of the rearguard, flanked by Diogo Dalot and Noussair Mazraoui on either side of the central defenders to protect goalkeeper Senne Lammens.

The role of Bruno Fernandes will also be intriguing to observe, as Carrick could deploy Youri Tielemans in an advanced central position and move the Portuguese playmaker out wide.

That tactical tweak would likely leave Mason Mount to operate as the third attacking midfielder, while Andrey Santos and Kobbie Mainoo potentially form a robust base in the engine room.

Leading the line will be Bryan Mbeumo, meaning Matheus Cunha is set to be limited to an impact role off the bench. In terms of absentees, Patrick Dorgu, Luke Shaw and Benjamin Sesko are definitely ruled out of the midweek encounter.

Furthermore, the Red Devils are sweating over the fitness of Marcus Rashford and Amad, with both attackers set to be rigorously assessed closer to kick-off.

Manchester United possible starting lineup:

Lammens; Dalot, Maguire, Martinez, Mazraoui; Mainoo, Santos; Fernandes, Tielemans, Mount; Mbeumo

#1859. Man City sign Enzo Fernandez for £125m to end transfer saga of the summer

Manchester City have equalled the British record transfer on deadline day after agreeing to pay £125m to sign midfielder Enzo Fernández from Chelsea.

The deal brings to an end the biggest saga of the summer and means that Enzo Maresca, the new City head coach, has landed his number one target.

City left it until the last day of the transfer window to strike an agreement after Chelsea decided that Fernández’s exit was in the best interests of the club. But a late move to replace the Argentine with Monaco midfielder Lamie Camara collapsed to the anger of the Premier League club, leaving Xabi Alonso one player light among his midfield options.

Having refused to meet Chelsea’s self-imposed deadline to sign Fernández for £120m earlier in the summer, City had to equal the £125m Liverpool paid Newcastle United for Alexander Isak 12 months earlier.

Fernández had made it clear that he wanted to leave Chelsea some time ago and was left out of Alonso’s squad for the victories last week over Luton Town, in the Carabao Cup, and Brighton.

Having initially wanted to join Real Madrid, Fernández set his heart on linking back up with Maresca at City. The pair share a close relationship and had kept in touch after Maresca left Chelsea at the start of the year.

This is the second time Fernández has become the most expensive player in British transfer history, having previously set the record when he joined Chelsea for £107m from Benfica in the 2023 winter window.

Introducing our new Argentinian Blue 🇦🇷🩵 pic.twitter.com/nEHQ1oM855

During his time at Chelsea, 25-year-old Fernández won the Club World Cup and the Europa Conference League but he was also at the centre of controversy.

In January 2025, Fernández posted a video of himself and some of his Argentina international team-mates singing an offensive song about France players of African origin after winning the Copa America. He apologised to his Chelsea team-mates and made a donation to an anti-discrimination charity, but was still made the team’s vice-captain.

Last season was Fernández’s best goalscoring campaign, as he netted 15 goals in all competitions for Chelsea but the club finished 10th in the Premier League table. In April, he was suspended for two games by the club for suggesting he would like to live in Madrid – which was perceived as a come and get me plea to Real Madrid.

He angered England fans with his celebration after scoring against Thomas Tuchel’s team in Argentina’s World Cup semi-final victory over England, before being sent-off in the final defeat by Spain.

Chelsea fans booed Fernández in pre-season, although the club’s travelling supporters sang his name when he was introduced as a substitute in the victory over Fulham at the start of this season.

Fernández thanked his team-mates and the Chelsea staff in an emotional farewell post on Instagram. He added: “I want you to know that these have not been easy days for me. Writing this is not easy either. The truth is, I haven’t been in a good place.

“Three years ago, Cobham and Stamford Bridge became home for me and my family. I grew attached to the people, to the shirt, and to the badge of this incredible club.

“Believe me when I say that, from the moment I arrived, I became obsessed with winning and with bringing this club every trophy that its history deserves. We suffered, we cried, I got angry many times, but we also celebrated titles and unforgettable victories. Together, through the good times and the difficult ones.

“I live football the same way I live my life: with passion and with all my heart. That is why I want you to know that I understand you. I truly understand you, from the bottom of my heart.

“But life is about making decisions, and right now I find myself having to make one of those difficult decisions. I’ve said it before, but I want to say it again: I have grown incredibly fond of this club. Chelsea will always have a place in my thoughts and, above all, in my heart.

“But I also understand how football works. I know how passionate you are, because I am the same. And if I were in your position, I would probably be thinking the same way.”

Proper City 🤩🩵 pic.twitter.com/TfRTZOnPrw

The sale of Fernández means that Chelsea have set a new British transfer record of their own, having secured more than £500m in sales and loan fees during the summer transfer window.

Chelsea set about spending some of the money made from the Fernández sale by agreeing a last-minute deal for Monaco midfielder Lamine Camara.

Monaco had rejected a bid of £38.5m from Chelsea on deadline day, but an improved offer of £47m was accepted late on Tuesday night, only to be called off by Monaco on the stroke of the 11pm deadline.

Chelsea had been able to complete a medical during negotiations and Camara agreed to a six-year contract with the option of a further year to bolster Alonso’s midfield options, but he will now not join the club.

Chelsea had also seen at least one offer for Bournemouth’s Alex Scott rejected this summer, while the club showed an interest in Roma’s Manu Kone and explored whether or not a move for Arsenal’s Martin Zubimendi would be possible earlier this month.

Chilly tonight... pic.twitter.com/VihgKCScfn

The 21-year-old midfielder who came through the ranks at Real Madrid has been signed from Stuttgart.

“We had been aware of Chema’s potential for sometime, and we are delighted to welcome him to the club, and look forward to working with him.”

Fernandez says: “Manchester City are the most successful club in England in recent times.

“Every player wants to be part of a club like this because everyone knows how well-run City are.

“I could not be happier to be here, and I am ready for the challenge of helping City continue winning trophies. This is a club built for success.

“If you look across the squad, City have quality in every area. I want to learn from my new teammates and become a better player.

Crystal Palace have agreed a deal to re-sign Ben Chilwell. The 29-year-old was on loan at Palace last year and deal struck with Strasbourg for him to leave French club and return to the Premier League.

Sunderland were involved in the most bewildering transfer of the summer on deadline day as they fought a day-long tug-of-war with Crystal Palace for winger Malick Fofana.

On a day of claims and counterclaims, Sunderland have finally triumphed in the battle to land the Belgium international just an hour before the deadline.

But despite their success, it was a transfer that will leave a sour taste in the mouth to many, with the player repeatedly changing his mind about which club he wanted to join

As the saga dragged on, it is understood Fofana had a medical in Lyon with both Sunderland and Crystal Palace given access to the information as he still could not decide which club to join as talks continued into the evening.

Sunderland had a bid of around £25m accepted by Lyon on Tuesday morning and thought they had an agreement with both the player and his agent on personal terms and fees only for Palace to make a late attempt to hijack the deal.

The London club’s manager, Pierre Sage, who worked with Fofana at Lyon, is thought to have personally intervened in an attempt to persuade the player to move to South London. By late afternoon, Palace appeared to have got their man having also offered more money to Lyon and higher wages to the player and fees to his agency.

Sunderland, though, refused to concede defeat and, according to reports in France, launched a counter proposal of their own led by French owners Kyril Louis-Dreyfus who flew to Lyon to try and clinch the deal.

At one stage, it was even claimed that the player had two different private jets waiting at the airport to take him to either London or the North East depending on who he elected to sign for.

That was later refuted, although it is understood the player did have a medical in Lyon that could be viewed by both clubs before he made up his mind. That gave his representatives more time to thrash the terms of a deal with both clubs.

However, having failed to board an earlier flight to Lyon after talks with Palace advanced, Sunderland’s late push belatedly persuaded the 21-year-old to head to Wearside, and he is due to be unveiled on Wednesday morning.

Arsenal had also been linked with the player earlier this week but were not willing to match the asking price for Fofana who they viewed as a project player.

After so long out of the game, Mudryk now has a coach who knows exactly how to get the best out of him. It might not work at all. Mudryk may need months to rediscover his match sharpness after so long out. But I am very excited to find out.

Once one of the fastest players in the world, Traore will join forces with another speedy forward in Pierre-Emerick Aubameyang to complete a vintage Premier League frontline...

Although much of the chatter today has related to Enzo Fernandez, a name that has cropped up a lot over the past hours has been that of Malick Fofana.

Sunderland had seemingly beaten Arsenal to the Lyon winger’s signature but reports have emerged that Crystal Palace are attempting to hijack Fofana’s Wearside move...

We’re still awaiting official confirmation of Mykhailo Mudryk’s loan move to Tottenham Hotspur. It would mean a reunion with Roberto De Zerbi, under whom the Ukrainian played at Shakhtar Donetsk.

When asked about Mudryk in 2022, the then Brighton head coach said: “Mykhailo has the potential for a top career. In my opinion, he can also win the Ballon d’Or. He is a player of the highest level but he is also very sensitive.”

De Zerbi added: “He needs affection. We will see if he matches his potential.”

Gabriel Jesus has completed his move from Arsenal to Barcelona in a deal worth about £9m. It’s a fantastic move for the Brazilian, who had declined in importance at Arsenal after a succession of serious injuries. Arsenal would have hoped for a higher fee for a player of his reputation but his enormous salary, believed to have been worth about £250,000 a week, was always going to be problematic as they looked for buyers.

When instinct calls, you answer. ☎️ pic.twitter.com/BgZktIcJ17

The 18-year-old centre-back will become a Chelsea player in the summer of 2027, but will spend the rest of this season on loan at Selhurst Park from Atalanta.

A brief update on Jayden Danns: he is going to stay at Liverpool, rather than accept a loan in Europe. There is some significance to this as, if you had read Telegraph Sport 10 days ago, you will know that Liverpool are in a position where for the first time in 134 years, a player born within the city might not represent them. Danns is the one who can keep the record going.

How is your team’s squad shaping up heading into the last stages of the window?

Sam Johnstone is heading to Celtic ahead of a loan deal from Wolves.

The 33-year-old, capped four times by England under Gareth Southgate, is travelling to Scotland this afternoon to completed the formalities of the deal including a medical.

Ainsley Maitland-Niles has emerged as a prime target for Everton, as they look to find a solution to their right-back conundrum. The former Arsenal defender, who is now at Lyon, has been the subject of a £5m offer and the indication is that he has now taken over from Kenny Tete as the preferred option. Everton, historically, have always pushed things to the wire on transfer deadline day and this one is proving to be no different.

His time to be a Villan... 🟣Aston Villa is delighted to announce the signing of Taylor Harwood-Bellis from Southampton 🏴󠁧󠁢󠁥󠁮󠁧󠁿 pic.twitter.com/snU0NgU8y1

With Woltemade travelling to undergo a medical with Juventus for a loan move from Newcastle, that would appear to shut off one potential exit route for Joshua Zirkzee. Juventus had been looking at a season long loan for Zirkzee. Fiorentina have also been keen on Zirkzee and made an offer to United of a loan plus €30m (£25.7m) buy option but the Netherlands forward turned down the chance to go there. United would be more likely to bring in another player, probably a left-back rather than a direct replacement, if Zirkzee was to go but time running out on that front.

United had hoped to sell Manuel Ugarte and Zirkzee this summer and were in the market for buyers for Marcus Rashford, but the window could close with all three staying put. Ugarte’s serious knee injury put paid to the Uruguay midfielder leaving and Rashford has been reintergrated in the squad after Barcelona opted against taking up an option to sign him permanently.

Benfica are in talks about loaning Argentina Under-23 forward Claudio Echeverri from Manchester City, It’s likely to be a season long loan with an option to buy if finalised.

Fabio Vieira has completed his move from Arsenal to Hamburg, in a deal believed to be worth about £9m. The Portuguese midfielder has never cut it in the Premier League and it is no surprise that Arsenal have cashed in. They paid more than £30m to sign him from Porto in 2022 but he has never come close to justifying the fee. In truth, it’s one of their worst transfers under Mikel Arteta.

Southampton forward Cameron Archer is on course to sign for Auxerre on a season-long loan.

Archer has been a target for a number of Championship clubs this summer but a deal has been problematic because of his £35,000-a-week wages.

It is understood Southampton have been demanding that his salary be paid in full, which has scared off interested clubs in the second tier.

Chelsea will hold off sanctioning Enzo Fernández’s move to Manchester City until they are confident of making at least one signing of their own.

Telegraph Sport understands that Chelsea have already rejected one proposal from City for Fernández during club-to-club talks and are demanding a fee and payment terms that are favourable to them.

Chelsea also have three separate targets of their own as potential deadline signings – Lamine Camara, Manu Kone and one mystery target from the Premier League.

Monaco have already rejected a £38.5m bid from Chelsea for Camara. Roma manager Gian Piero Gasperini wants to keep Kone, although negotiations continue. And there is a third target from the Premier League, who is not believed to be Morgan Gibbs-White.

Chelsea must make significant progress on one of their targets before they will sanction Fernández’s sale – and City must make another bid that is more favourable to the club.

Monaco have rejected an opening €45m bid from Chelsea for midfielder Lamine Camara. It now remains to be seen if the club increase that offer.

Sunderland have been trying to sign a winger all summer and it appears that they have finally got their man in Lyon’s Malick Fofana.

Arsenal had been linked with a move for the 21-year old Belgium international.

The Argentina forward missed three training sessions last week and was not included in Diego Simeone’s squad that travelled to Sevilla last weekend.

Plenty of chatter about the future of Roma midfielder Manu Koné, who is linked with a move to Chelsea. The France international would be a strong acquisition for Xabi Alonso, but could his potential signing precede an Enzo Fernández exit? All will be revealed in due course...

Of Koné, former France manager Didier Deschamps said: “He’s very effective at winning the ball back, but he shouldn’t be limited to that role of defensive midfielder, because he also makes a difference in his use of the ball.”

Austria centre-back David Affengruber has emerged as potential deadline-day deal for Fulham as they look to bolster Alvaro Arbeloa’s defence.

The Elche player has been in La Liga for two years playing regularly and fits the data model at Craven Cottage.

Fulham are also trying deals for Real Madrid’s Manuel Angel and Eintracht Frankfurt’s Hugo Larsson as midfield options.

Sunderland are expected to complete the signing of centre-back Kevin Danso from Tottenham Hotspur with the player travelling to Wearside last night for the first part of his medical.

The Austria international will initially join on loan with an obligation to make the move permanent for £25m next year.

Danso had made it clear he wanted to leave Tottenham this summer in search of regular first-team football.

Eintracht Frankfurt are in talks with Nottingham Forest over another loan move for forward Arnaud Kalimuendo.

Frankfurt signed the Frenchman on loan in January and are negotiating a return for Forest’s £26m signing from Rennes.

Oliver Glasner, Forest’s head coach, had been intent on keeping Kalimuendo but it is understood Frankfurt’s strong interest has altered the club’s thinking.

Morato, the centre-back, is expected to join West Ham United on loan.

Forest are exploring potential signings but are determined to stay calm and only pursue deals that make financial sense. A winger and a No 6 are the two priority targets if there are deals to be done.

On Tuesday evening, the Tottenham and Brazil forward posted an emotional message on Instagram amid reports of a possible move back to Everton.

He wrote: “After everything I’ve been through in recent years, I decided that never again would others decide my future for me.

“I went through a lot of bad things during this time, and almost all of them happened because of decisions made by other people. Pressure, threats, retaliation – none of that scares me. I’ve been through worse, believe me!

“I have always made it clear at every opportunity that my departure to another place would also have to be good for the club. If it wasn’t, I would never accept it... just as I didn’t accept it when everything here was falling apart and they needed me.”

Richarlison added: “I stayed and gave my all. So, I hope they treat my situation with the same respect that I have always had for Spurs and for all the people who worked with me during this period. Just don’t try to decide for me.”

“If Spurs and Everton reach an agreement, I will return to the club of my heart. My intention was indeed to go back to the place where I was very happy.

“But negotiations were being done the way other people wanted, and it won’t be that way anymore. Despite all this turmoil, I have a contract with Spurs and I will remain at the club’s disposal.”

It will be good news for Arsenal if Folarin Balogun completes his £40m move to Everton today. When Arsenal sold Balogun to Monaco in 2023, they negotiated a sell-on clause of 17.5 per cent. According to my maths, that means Arsenal will get £7m from this transfer. Not to be sniffed at!

Hull City are close to agreeing a fee of around £7.5m for Stoke City winger Sorba Thomas.

The Wales international has been a long-term target for Hull and negotiations are now approaching a conclusion.

Thomas has been pushing a move through and is expected to leave Stoke after one full season.

As has become the norm this summer Acun Ilicali has posted a cryptic message on X, which has prompted speculation among Hull City fans. The club has been linked with Everton holding midfielder Tim Iroegbunam.

Will Barcola hit the ground running at Anfield? The France winger registered 20 goal contributions in 49 games for Paris St-Germain last season.

A warm welcome from the skipper 😍 pic.twitter.com/95EAqUjYBn

The La Masia graduate secures a permanent move to Germany. Who knows how his career in England would have panned out had Chelsea not recalled him 25 days into his Sunderland loan at the beginning of last season...

Marc Guiu has completed a permanent transfer to Bundesliga side RB Leipzig. Everyone at Chelsea would like to thank Marc for his efforts during his time at the club and wish him every success as he begins the next chapter of his career with RB Leipzig.

What a couple of weeks it has been for Robert Sanchez. He came into this season as Chelsea’s No 1, but after a difficult start to the campaign and Emi Martinez’s arrival, reports suggest he could be moving away from Stamford Bridge on loan. Cesc Fabregas’s Como appears the probable destination.

Trevoh Chalobah, who left Chelsea for Como last month, has taken to his “secondary” Instagram account to post the following picture...

Meanwhile, as reported by Telegraph Sport yesterday, striker flop Nick Woltemade is moving to Juventus on a season-long loan. The club’s record signing from as year ago at £64m is moving to Turin for a £3.5m loan fee with the Serie A squad covering the full cost of his wages.

Newcastle will complete the £51m signing of forward Matias Fernandez-Pardo from Lille today but that is expected to be it in terms of incomings.

The Belgium international will become the club’s eighth signing of the summer and his versatility – he can play as a centre forward, a No 10 or out wide – means there are no more gaps to fill in the squad.

In an ideal world, Newcastle would have liked to sign another defender but none of their targets were still on the market. With Dan Burn due to return from injury in a few weeks, they have four centre-backs while new arrival Amar Dedic can play on both sides as a full-back.

In terms of outgoings, Joe Willock and Jacob Murphy are expected to stay at the club despite interest from Nottingham Forest and Besiktas. Young striker Sean Neave will be allowed to leave on loan. The 19-year-old has offers from clubs in the Championship and League One but Newcastle want him to go somewhere he has the best chance of getting regular first-team football.

City have been this summer’s selling kings and have had six players leave the club in deals worth more than £45m. Compare that to the summer when Pep Guardiola first arrived at the club, in 2016, when City generated just £23m from sales and made losses on Edin Dzeko and Stevan Jovetic, while Martín Demichelis departed on a free transfer.

Fast forward to this summer and more than £300m worth of players have been sold, with a further £60m arriving at the end of the season when Omar Marmoush’s loan to Tottenham Hotspur becomes permanent.

Given how Jaissle wants Newcastle to play, it is plain to see why Fernandez-Pardo appeals to him. Quick, direct and only 21 – he would surely fit right in at St James’ Park.

A post shared by Ligue 1 McDonald's (@ligue1mcdonalds)

The Leeds wide man has a medical booked with Fiorentina today. He made a handful of appearances for Daniel Farke’s side during pre-season but has not featured since the start of the 2026-27 campaign.

✈️ L'arrivo di Gnonto a Firenze ⚜️ pic.twitter.com/nEFngsyxQP

Very unlikely that Liverpool will be doing any major incoming business but there may yet be some departures. Jayden Danns, who broke through three years ago and played in the 2024 League Cup final defeat of Chelsea, is attracting interest from clubs in Europe, who want to take him on loan. Danns, a promising striker, has had injury issues and is working his way back to full fitness but his long-term ambition is to prove to Andoni Iraola that he can be part of his squad.

Fax machines are whirring as the clock continues to tick towards the transfer deadline, but who does your club need to sign? Let us know in the comments below!

Aston Villa are to confirm the signings of £50m winger Ibrahim Mbaye and £25m centre-back Taylor Harwood-Bellis this morning.

Mbaye and Harwood-Bellis takes the number of Villa’s signings this summer to 10, with Unai Emery ruling out any more additions after the 1-0 defeat by Arsenal last night.

Emery also disclosed that forward Tammy Abraham will be staying at Villa Park, amid interest from Ipswich Town.

The one player who could leave today is Jamaica international Leon Bailey, who has interest from clubs in Europe, and Hull City.

Nottingham Forest can confirm Omari Hutchinson has joined AC Milan on a season-long loan deal, with the Italian club holding an option to make the transfer permanent.Everyone at Nottingham Forest wishes Omari all the best for his time in Italy. pic.twitter.com/fSv1uNGh2Y

Fulham remain locked in discussions with Rayo Vallecano to agree a fee for right-back Andrei Ratiu, with the Romania international having confirmed he wants to join Alvaro Arbeloa’s side. The spin-off with this deal is that it will accelerate Kenny Tete’s switch to Everton, for a fee in the region of £9.5m.

On the subject of right-backs, Nathan Patterson, who has had a difficult time at Everton, has been granted permission to travel to Italy to undergo a medical with Torino.

Matias Fernandez-Pardo is on the verge of joining Newcastle United, and Luke Edwards reported that the forward’s arrival is likely to pave the way for Nick Woltemade’s departure.

The German enjoyed a fruitful start to life in England after signing last summer, scoring seven Premier League goals before the turn of the year, but could only manage one goal in the second half of the season. While Eddie Howe experimented with Woltemade in a more withdrawn No 10 role, there was a clear drop-off in his game-time after Christmas.

Newcastle are ready to pay around £51m to sign Fernandez-Pardo after holding face-to-face talks with Lille last week. The 21-year-old is a versatile attacker and Newcastle identified him as a top target months ago. If they can complete a deal, it could speed up the departure of Nick Woltemade, who is wanted by Juventus.

The Brazilian has asked to leave Spurs and has been linked to a move back to Everton. However, his hopes of returning to Merseyside may have taken a hit on Monday night, when Everton agreed a £40m deal with Monaco for striker Folarin Balogun.

Brighton are keen to sign Azeez from Millwall and have made multiple offers for the forward. Millwall want at least £15m for Azeez, who scored 11 goals in the Championship last season. Ipswich Town have previously shown interest in Azeez.

Leeds are signing Melvin Bard on loan from Nice. One-season deal for the 25-year-old who will compete for a place in the first-team under Daniel Farke.

We’re expecting four departures from Arsenal today. Nwaneri to Dortmund on loan (see my colleague Mike McGrath’s post below), Gabriel Martinelli to Al-Hilal, Gabriel Jesus to Barcelona and Fabio Vieira to Hamburg. Those deals should raise around £70m.

Will there be any incomings? The Julian Alvarez situation seems unlikely to develop in Arsenal’s favour, barring a dramatic change of heart. As reported by Telegraph Sport yesterday, Lyon winger Malick Fofana is a potential option.

Borussia Dortmund have been trying to close out a loan deal for Arsenal winger Ethan Nwaneri, as reported by Telegraph Sport yesterday. The German club have previously attempted to land the 19-year-old and this time want him on a deal for the season.

It is expected to be another busy deadline day in the Premier League, with many clubs still hoping to finalise deals before the transfer window shuts at 11pm. Here, Telegraph Sport identifies 10 potential high-profile moves that could yet go through.

This has been the most dramatic and relentless saga of the European transfer window. The situation, as far as we understand it, is as follows: Barcelona want Alvarez and Alvarez wants Barcelona, but Atletico Madrid refuse to sell him to Barcelona. Arsenal want Alvarez, and Atletico are more open to selling him to Arsenal, but Alvarez only wants Barcelona. For a move to happen, it will require one party to change their mind. Either Atletico decides to sell to Barcelona, or Alvarez decides he will join Arsenal.

Another long-running saga. Chelsea are well aware of City’s interest in Fernandez but want a massive fee for the Argentina international, having initially valued him at £120m. City have the cash and the space in the squad after saying goodbye to Rodri, Tijani Reijnders, Nico Gonzalez and Bernardo Silva this summer. Fernandez has not featured in Chelsea’s last two games.

As reported by Telegraph Sport last week, Chelsea have identified Monaco midfielder Camara as a target amid the uncertainty over Fernandez’s future. French reports on Monday suggested the move may have stalled, however. The clock is ticking.

Spurs had been working on a deal to sign Ndiaye from Everton but they now appear to have fallen behind City in the race for the winger, as a consequence of City failing in their attempt to sign Cody Gakpo from Liverpool. City are ready to complete the hijack on deadline day.

A deal that, as of Monday night, is regarded as unlikely to happen. As with their interest in Brighton’s Yankuba Minteh, Liverpool have so far been unable to strike a deal with Crystal Palace for Sarr, who scored 21 goals in 45 games last season. Liverpool would only allow Gakpo to leave if a replacement, such as Sarr, can be signed.

Burnley are one of a host of Championship clubs who are interested in the young Manchester United left-back Harry Amass. There have been talks over a potential permanent deal but a loan cannot be ruled out. The 19-year-old joined United from Watford in 2023.

Everton have reached an agreement with Manchester City to sign Jack Grealish on another season long loan. It has been a very busy summer of outgoings at City and Grealish will be the latest to depart as he prepares to return to Merseyside. He started well at Everton last season before injury in January derailed his campaign.

A big year ahead for the English midfielder.

Tottenham are set to complete a double deal for Chelsea pair Mykhailo Mudryk and Tosin Adarabioyo after missing out on Iliman Ndiaye.

Spurs will take Mudryk on loan for the season having seen their attempt to land Ndiaye fail when Manchester City agreed a £65m deal with Everton.

Mudryk, 25, worked with Spurs head coach Roberto De Zerbi at Shakthtar Donetsk, in the winger’s homeland Ukraine, before his £85m move to Chelsea in 2023.

Leeds United had shown interest but instead he will be reunited with De Zerbi, effectively taking Ndiaye’s place as a wide-forward option.

Adarabioyo will be a permanent deal to Spurs as they are not allowed to loan two players from a Premier League club.

Good morning and welcome to live coverage of transfer deadline day. We are deep into stoppage time in this summer window and we will bring you the key developments as teams scramble to get last-minute deals over the line before the full-time whistle blows at 11pm.

Enzo Fernández remains a City target, and his omission from Xabi Alonso’s match-day squad against Brighton and Hove Albion on Sunday has only added weight to the feeling that he might reunite with former Chelsea head coach Enzo Maresca. City would be required to meet the Londoners’ £120m asking price, which is just shy of Alexander Isak’s £125m British record fee.

Meanwhile, Julián Alvarez’s situation at Atlético Madrid continues to be monitored by Arsenal. The Argentina forward’s dream move to Barcelona appears a no-goer as Atlético remain steadfast in their refusal to sell to their La Liga rivals. While this could bring Arsenal into the picture, it is understood that Alvarez – who missed three training sessions last week and did not travel to Sevilla with Diego Simeone’s squad on Saturday – is not pursuing a return to England.

A Mohamed Salah-shaped hole on Liverpool’s right flank has been filled by Bradley Barcola after the club agreed a £123m deal with Paris St-Germain. His signing looked as though it might trigger Cody Gakpo’s move away from Anfield as the winger had been linked with a move to Manchester City, but it appears that the Netherlands international will stay put. Maresca’s side have instead hijacked Spurs’ move for Iliman Ndiaye, and the north London outfit pivoted to take Myhailo Mudryk and Tosin Adarabioyo from Chelsea, on loan and permanent deals respectively. Liverpool could yet swoop for Brighton’s Yankuba Minteh or Ismaïla Sarr.

Newcastle United appeared to have reached their nadir this summer after Anthony Gordon, Sandro Tonali, Bruno Guimarães and Eddie Howe departed, but Matthias Jaissle has breathed life into St James’ Park by delivering an exciting brand of football that leans on the team’s explosive pace in forward positions. Lille’s Matias Fernandez-Pardo would fit this system and is on the brink of joining Newcastle in a deal worth £51m, which could signal Nick Woltemade’s exit.

Barcola is the window’s most expensive acquisition, followed by Morgan Rogers who was prised away from Aston Villa to the tune of £118m, and has already hit the ground running for the Londoners. He cost £2m more than his England team-mate Elliot Anderson, who swapped Nottingham Forest for Manchester City. Elite midfielders have proved a gilded commodity with seven of the Premier League’s top 10 most expensive acquisitions coming in the middle of the park. The departures of Rodri, Casemiro and others will have played their part.

Praying for a deadline-day saviour or counting down the seconds until the window slams shut on directors of football hoping to lure away your club’s next big thing? Let us know in the comments and join the conversation as the day unfolds.

#1858. Rio Ferdinand says Man Utd should have signed ‘top player’ Ezri Konsa before Arsenal

Rio Ferdinand wishes Manchester United had signed ‘top player’ Ezri Konsa before his £55m move to Arsenal.

Konsa has enjoyed a brilliant start to his Gunners career following a big-money move from Aston Villa over the summer.

The 29-year-old came straight into Mikel Arteta’s team due to William Saliba’s injury lay-off and has helped Arsenal win 13 of their 16 games so far this season.

Konsa produced another impressive display on Sunday as Arsenal beat Liverpool 1-0 to clinch their first victory at Anfield since 2012.

Sign up to our daily football newsletter, pick your team and get the latest news sent directly to your inbox every morning.

Ferdinand told his 18-year-old son Tate, who is a centre-back in the Brighton academy, to watch Konsa against Liverpool, such is his admiration for the England star.

And the Manchester United legend even wishes his former club had signed Konsa before his move to the reigning Premier League champions.

Ferdinand expects Saliba to come straight back into the team once fit but says Konsa could well move to right-back, a position he knows well, and rival Jurrien Timber for a place in the side.

‘I think William Saliba is one of those guys that you have to find room for in the team,’ Ferdinand said on his YouTube channel when asked whether Konsa could keep Saliba out of the Arsenal XI. ‘He’s that good, he’s top.

‘I said to my son yesterday, “watch Ezri Konsa”, because everything he does is efficient. That’s a great problem for Mikel Arteta to have.

Use AI to go deeper into the stories you care about – powered by Metro and trusted publications.

‘I wouldn’t be surprised if Konsa goes back to right-back once Saliba comes back. I wouldn’t be surprised because Konsa is top.

To view this video please enable JavaScript, and consider upgrading to a web browser that supports HTML5 video

‘He’s a top, top player and another one I thought Manchester United should have got because he’s a top player.

‘He’s giving Mikel Arteta some big decisions to make and big headaches because he’s slipped in seamlessly and put in some big performances

Arteta described the performance of his Arsenal team as ‘remarkable’ after they ended their long wait for a win at Anfield.

‘So happy, so proud, full of energy,’ Arteta said. ‘What can I say – it’s a proud moment for everybody attached with the football club.

‘It’s been 14 years waiting for this moment, and we did it in very special circumstances after the defeat against Fleetwood in a way we didn’t deserve four days ago.

‘And now having to come to Anfield, making sure everybody is convinced, prepared and ready to navigate a football match, that is going to have very difficult moments, some big opportunities and when they come, you need to be ready to grab them.

#1857. Jack Grealish Everton return unclear as David Moyes speaks out on his future

When Jack Grealish will return to the Everton squad remains unclear as manager David Moyes hinted it was not just a lack of match fitness that left him unavailable against Newcastle on Monday night.

The England international has missed Everton’s last three games as he sat out a Premier League clash with Arsenal through illness and then was left out of a Carabao Cup meeting with Newcastle after a breach of club discipline.

That breach is believed to be an unauthorised absence from training, for which he was punished as he was not involved in the 3-1 win on October 29.

The Toffees faced the Magpies again on Monday, this time in the Premier League, with Grealish absent but this time the club said it was a fitness issue.

Sign up to our daily football newsletter, pick your team and get the latest news sent directly to your inbox every morning.

An Everton statement read on Monday: ‘Jack Grealish is not match fit and therefore not part of tonight’s squad.’

A Thierno Barry goal meant Everton made it two wins over Newcastle in Grealish’s absence as they climbed to seventh in the Premier League table.

Moyes was asked about the situation with the 31-year-old and he seemed to suggest that he was not just unavailable due to match fitness, as the club had stated.

‘He’s unavailable at the moment and we’ll make a decision with the club when we think that availability comes back,’ said the Scot.

Asked if his unavailability was due to lacking match fitness, Moyes said: ‘All I’m giving out is he’s unavailable at the moment.’

Use AI to go deeper into the stories you care about – powered by Metro and trusted publications.

On whether the issue of ill-discipline is now over and done with and if he could comment on the matter, the manager said: ‘No, I can’t comment on that.’

Moyes was giving little away as he said he didn’t yet know whether Grealish would be available when Everton host Coventry City in the Premier League on Friday night.

However, he was clear when asked of the possibility of a return at some stage and a future for the winger at the club, saying: ‘Of course there is, yes.’

Grealish has made five Premier League appearances for Everton this season after returning for a second spell on loan from Manchester City.

After two substitute appearances he started the games against Ipswich Town, Hull City and Chelsea before his ongoing absence began.

Reportedly Everton’s highest-paid player, he has not found form yet this campaign, yet to register a goal or an assist.

#1856. Sky: From Galliani to Kaka – Cardinale treated Milan figures to dinner to explain project

Gerry Cardinale hosted a dinner on the eve of the big derby clash between AC Milan and Inter, explaining his projects to Adriano Galliani, Ricky Kaka, Ezio Simonelli and many others.

Cardinale has been in Italy for the last week or so, attending the new stadium unveiling as well as the games against Udinese and Bologna. Tonight, he will be at San Siro for the derby and to mark the big occasion, he hosted a big dinner last night.

Read SempreMilan ad-free and get access to exclusive news. Click here for a free trial!

According to Peppe Di Stefano of Sky, as relayed by MilanVibes, Cardinale invited about 60 people to dinner. It wasn’t just an opportunity to catch up, but also for the American to explain what he has planned for Milan, seeking the support of some club legends.

As mentioned at the top, the likes of Galliani, Kaka and the Serie A president Simonelli attended the dinner. Other notable Milan legends present were Marcel Desailly, Serginho, Cristian Brocchi, Mathieu Flamini, Mauro Tassotti, Filippo Galli and Daniele Massaro.

It was definitely nice to see Galliani turn up at the dinner, especially since he bumped into Kaka outside and we thus got a chance to see their warm embrace. The two still have a great relationship after experiencing so much success together over the years.

#1855. Bodo/Glimt vs Lille - prediction, team news, lineups

By Anthony Nolan | 01 Nov 2026 23:59, Last updated: 03 Nov 2026 14:13

Sensing an opportunity to snatch a win in the Champions League's league-phase, Bodo/Glimt will welcome Lille to Aspmyra Stadion on Tuesday.

Glimt are desperate to avoid a third defeat in four continental games, though Les Dogues are looking to build on their win last time out by collecting their first points in the competition.

Kjetil Knutsen's Bodo are currently embroiled in a tense title race at the summit of Norway's Eliteserien, and they will be hoping that their 3-2 triumph over rivals Viking FK can inspire them to victory in midweek.

Glimt raced into an early two-goal lead during Friday's top-of-the-table showdown, only for Viking to claw their way back to 2-2 with less than 40 minutes on the clock.

However, Knutsen's side got their noses back in front via Jens Hauge moments later and were able to hold out to beat the reigning champions and draw level on points in second, with both teams' managers being sent off before the interval.

Inspired by their success in that heated clash, Bodo - who currently sit 28th in the league-phase table - will be eyeing a spot in the Champions League's top 24 by the end of the matchweek.

In order to rise through the ranks, Glimt will need to bounce back from a 4-3 defeat to Napoli last time out in Europe, though they will be buoyed by facing one of the competition's strugglers on home turf.

Meanwhile, Davide Ancelotti's Lille have produced a strong campaign overall, but it would be fair to say that they have stumbled over the past month.

Prior to their 1-0 victory against Lens on Friday, Les Dogues had produced a four-game winless run across all competitions, losing twice and drawing twice.

Those defeats were both in the Champions League, with Ancelotti's men beaten 3-0 by Arsenal at the Emirates Stadium on October 10, and 4-2 by Galatasaray at home two weeks ago.

To make matters worse, Lille are still waiting for their first Champions League points this term and sit 35th in the table, three shy of the top 24 and six behind the top eight.

That being said, the club's continental strife belies the fact that Les Dogues are second only to Paris Saint-Germain in Ligue 1 so far, and are not to be underestimated on Tuesday after scoring in all but one of their 13 matches this season.

Bodo will be without goalkeepers Julian Faye Lund and Isak Sjong due to respective injuries, though Nikita Haikin should be on hand to continue between the sticks.

Midfielder Hakon Evjen is also sidelined with a knee injury, while August Mikkelsen is dealing with a groin issue, so Patrick Berg and Sondre Fet could start in the centre of the park, platforming a strike partnership of Ole Didrik Blomberg and Andreas Helmersen.

As for Lille, they are missing the versatile Ethan Mbappe, who is serving the final game of his suspension following a red card against Real Betis on matchday one, while Hamza Igamane has a knee injury, and fellow striker Ayase Ueda is working his way back from a foot injury.

In their absence, 40-year-old Olivier Giroud could lead the line on Tuesday, supported by a trio of Dilane Bakwa, Hakon Haraldsson and Soriba Diaoune.

Elsewhere, right-back Tiago Santos suffered an anterior cruciate ligament tear and meniscus damage against Le Havre on October 12, so 18-year-old Maxima Goffi looks set to start in midweek.

Haikin; Sjovold, Bjortuft, Gundersen, Bjorkan; Auklend, Fet, Berg, Hauge; Blomberg, Helmersen

Ozer; Goffi, Ngoy, Alexsandro, Perraud; Andre, Bentaleb; Bakwa, Haraldsson, Diaoune; Giroud

Bodo may have lost two of their three Champions League matches so far, but they will be inspired by their victory over Viking and could deliver a strong performance in midweek.

However, Lille will be desperate to get off the mark in the competition, and may hold Glimt to a draw after ending their winless run.

#1854. Tenerife striker Jesus de Miguel, 30, dies after collision with goalkeeper

Jesus de Miguel has died after a collision during Tenerife’s match against Andorra on Monday evening.

The 30-year-old suffered head and chest injuries following a collision with Andorra goalkeeper Jesus Owono, who was sent off the challenge near the halfway line.

Owono had sprinted from his goal to clear a long ball when his knee collided with De Miguel’s chest.

De Miguel rolled on the floor immediately after impact but was then motionless on his back as several players urgently signalled for medical help.

Sign up to our daily football newsletter, pick your team and get the latest news sent directly to your inbox every morning.

The referee showed Owono a red card before the match was abandoned.

An initial statement from Tenerife on Monday night said that De Miguel was ‘stable’ in hospital.

But a second update from the Spanish club in the early hours of Tuesday morning said that De Miguel’s ‘medical condition has worsened neurologically’.

Later on Tuesday morning, Tenerife announced that De Miguel has died.

Tenerife’s statement said: ‘Heartbroken, with a lump in our throats and unable to believe this is true, CD Tenerife announces the tragic death, this Tuesday, November 3, 2026, at 8:00 a.m., of Jesús de Miguel Alameda.

Use AI to go deeper into the stories you care about – powered by Metro and trusted publications.

‘There are no words of comfort; there is absolutely nothing that can lessen this overwhelming sadness. We stand with his grieving family, with his loved ones, with all of Tenerife who mourn this cruel loss today.

Andorra also released a statement which read: ‘With broken hearts and devastated, we wish to send our deepest condolences to the family of Jesús de Miguel, all his teammates, friends, and CD Tenerife. May he rest in peace.’

In response to Tenerife’s statement confirming De Miguel’s death, former Barcelona defender Gerard Pique, who is now the president of Andorra FC, wrote on X: ‘I am so sorry. Rest in peace, Jesus.’
