#1853. Man Utd boost as £33m left-back decides he’s ‘open’ to January transfer

Barcelona misfit Alejandro Balde is reportedly ‘open’ to leaving the club in January amid strong interest from Manchester United.

Balde joined Barca at the age of just eight after impressing in Espanyol’s youth ranks and would go on to break into the Catalan giants’ first-team in 2021.

The 23-year-old left-back has since made a total of 172 appearances in all competitions for Barca while helping the club win seven pieces of silverware, including three La Liga titles.

However, Balde has badly struggled for regular playing time under head coach Hansi Flick, with all four of his appearances this season coming from the substitutes bench.

Sign up to our daily football newsletter, pick your team and get the latest news sent directly to your inbox every morning.

Balde currently finds himself behind both Joao Cancelo and Xavi Espart in the pecking order at the Camp Nou and the Spain international’s career appears to be at a crossroads.

According to Spanish publication Mundo Deportivo, Barca’s coaching staff are of the belief that Balde is prone to ‘losing focus’ and is unable to read the game well when it comes to pressing.

‘Balde doesn’t have the confidence he needs in his game right now, nor the conviction,’ Flick told reporters ahead of Barca’s 6-1 victory over Alaves last weekend.

It’s claimed the situation has left Balde ‘open’ to the prospect of moving on from Barca, with the out-of-favour full-back ‘beginning to accept’ that this is likely his only route back to playing consistently.

Balde is said to have grown ‘upset’ as he expected Flick to have been direct and honest with him over his limited minutes, as the German supposedly had been with the likes of Marc Casado and Hector Fort.

Use AI to go deeper into the stories you care about – powered by Metro and trusted publications.

The report adds that ‘everything Balde has heard about his situation has come through press conferences’ and the defender is now strongly considering a move as early as this winter, with Manchester United emerging as a possible destination.

Balde is ‘attracted’ by the idea of testing himself in the Premier League and his camp are ready to listen to offers from potential suitors.

He has ‘learned lessons’ from his close friend Ansu Fati, who spent a number of years waiting for opportunities at Barca without managing to nail down regular game-time.

It is believed a bid in the region of €40million (£33m) could be enough to secure a deal for Balde when the January transfer window opens for business.

There are 18 months remaining on Balde’s current contract with the reigning Spanish champions.

Manchester United had been actively looking to strengthen at left-back in the summer in order to provide support and competition for Luke Shaw, the club’s only specialist in the position other than academy product Harry Amass.

But United ultimately failed to bolster their full-back options which has come back to bite them already this season, with Shaw sidelined for the last month through injury.

Diogo Dalot has therefore been forced to fill in as a makeshift left-back during United’s miserable winless streak under an increasingly under-pressure Michael Carrick.

It’s understood Lewis Hall had been identified as United’s number one left-back target ahead of the 2026/27 campaign, but Newcastle made it clear the England international would not be sold for anything other than an astronomical price.

Hall would go on to put pen to paper on a new long-term deal at St James’ Park, tying him to the Magpies until 2031.

Bournemouth’s Adrien Truffert, Fulham’s Antonee Robinson, RB Leipzig’s David Raum and Crystal Palace’s Tyrick Mitchell have also been linked with the Red Devils in recent months.

#1852. Wayne Rooney slams ‘horrendous’ Man Utd star who Michael Carrick is still backing

Wayne Rooney has blasted Lisandro Martinez for his ‘horrendous’ mistake for Chelsea’s opening goal in their victory over Manchester United.

United are now nine games without a win after a 2-0 defeat to Chelsea at Stamford Bridge on Saturday afternoon.

Martinez was sent off midway through the second-half just minutes after he was booked for raising his elbow and catching Wesley Fofana while defending a corner.

The Argentina international has been widely condemned for his reckless actions which came just weeks after he publicly blasted the club following the Champions League defeat to Atletico Madrid.

Sign up to our daily football newsletter, pick your team and get the latest news sent directly to your inbox every morning.

While firmly among those unimpressed with Martinez’s conduct for the sending off, former United captain Rooney was equally appalled by his role in Chelsea’s opener.

Morgan Rogers drove through United’s midfield and defence with Andrey Santos, Harry Maguire and Martinez all failing to stop him.

Rooney blasted the former Ajax star for his meek attempts to deal with Rogers’ run and insisted it was Chelsea’s opening goal that sparked United’s downfall.

‘The first goal for me was a killer for everyone,’ Rooney told The United Stand.

‘Rogers picks the ball up and just runs in a straight line. Yoro is out of position which can happen because there was a turnover. Maguire does the right thing initially but the closer Rogers gets, he has to get him and leave him out wide.

Use AI to go deeper into the stories you care about – powered by Metro and trusted publications.

‘And then Martinez comes across – his attempt at a tackle is horrendous, you wouldn’t want school boys doing that.

‘He goes in and just touches Rogers, he doesn’t put any force into it, that’s where you put your body across and try knock him. He just waves his arm at him and lets him go through. That goal was horrendous.’

United return to action against Roma in the Champions League tonight with Carrick insisting this week he has no concerns over Martinez’s commitment to the cause.

‘I’ve got no concerns about commitment at all,’ Carrick told a news conference on Tuesday.

‘The dressing room is a good, good place,’ the United boss said. ‘I’ve said it before, the commitment of the players to the club, to me, to each other is I don’t question that at all.

‘We need to play better, we can make better decisions, but commitment’s not a thing at all.’

#1851. Arsenal transfer news: Gunners in 'contact' with new Real Madrid star ahead of January after moving on from Vinicius Junior

By Lewis Nolan | 02 Nov 2026 00:17

Arsenal are in contact with Real Madrid attacker Endrick as a January move becomes more realistic, the newest report has revealed.

The Gunners will be revelling in their crucial 1-0 win against Liverpool at Anfield on Sunday, with that result taking them to first place in the Premier League.

Mikel Arteta's side had to rely on their defence for much of the game due to the pressure their hosts applied, but the game would have been more comfortable if they had better forwards on the pitch.

The January transfer window is fast approaching, and many supporters are keen for the club to make a marquee addition so that they do not have to rely too heavily on Bukayo Saka in the second half of the season.

Arteta was said to have been keen on Real Madrid forward Vinicius Junior in the summer transfer window, though that move was always unlikely.

However, TEAMtalk claim that Arsenal are in contact with the representatives of Real attacker Endrick, who has grown increasingly frustrated by his playing time in Spain and would be open to a January move.

Endrick was reportedly of interest to many teams in the Premier League over the summer, and he may regret staying in Spain given he has played just 108 minutes for Real Madrid in all competitions.

The 20-year-old move to Lyon on loan last January, playing 21 times, scoring eight goals and providing seven assists.

One of the Brazilian's best assets is his ability to cross into the penalty area, while he is also capable of dribbling past opposition defenders before unleashing a shot at goal.

Endrick is also capable of playing across the frontline, and he could be an invaluable option for Arteta, who may need to rotate his attack considerably over the coming months in order to avoid injuries occuring.

While most have acknowledged that Arsenal's attack has been subpar for some time, the prospect of the Gunners adding an elite attacker to their ranks should be frightening.

The Londoners have already won eight of their first nine Premier League games, conceding just five times, and they have been nearly flawless at the back.

Should Arteta add a new dynamic to their attack, in January or the summer, then the club could be set for a period of dominance, especially if Manchester City are relegated or expelled for breaching the league's spending rules.

Rice’s surging run and inch-perfect cross set up Kai Havertz for the winner as Mikel Arteta’s side ground out a hard-fought 1-0 win at Anfield.

The Arsenal midfielder was named Player of the Match for his all-action display, with Jamie Carragher suggesting afterwards that the 27-year-old is the ‘best central midfielder in the Premier League’.

Scholes, meanwhile, believes that Rice showed a different, more instinctive side to his game on Sunday, and believes ‘nobody can live’ with the Englishman if he continues playing in that vein.

‘If he decides to just play one and two touch and run, he’ll be virtually unplayable, almost in a Steven Gerrard type of way.

#1848. Tottenham and Newcastle-linked striker talks up move to ‘big club’

Villarreal striker Georges Mikautadze has been linked with a move away from the Spanish side and feels he is ‘ready to go to a big club’.

The 26-year-old has had an interesting career path so far, breaking through at French side Metz before earning a move to Ajax which did not make out and he returned to his first professional club.

The Georgia international would then move to Lyon in 2024 and switched again the following year as he joined Villarreal.

He scored 15 goals in all competitions last season and has netted five so far in this campaign, including the opener in the 4-3 defeat at Liverpool in the Champions League last month.

Sign up to our daily football newsletter, pick your team and get the latest news sent directly to your inbox every morning.

Both Tottenham and Newcastle have been credited with interest in Mikautadze before, while Barcelona are also thought to like the forward.

He is not shy in admitting that he fancies a step up and feels ready to do just that.

‘I think I’m ready to go to a big club,’ Mikautade told L’Equipe. ‘I have everything I need and I try to show it every time. I just maybe need a little more time.’

Specifically responding to Barcelona’s interest in him, he said: ‘Yes, it’s flattering and it motivates me even more. It also means that the work is being done well.

‘As a child, ever since the Xavi-Iniesta-Busquets era and the MSN [Messi-Suarez-Neymar] trio, I’ve been a Barca supporter. But I hadn’t really thought about it.’

Use AI to go deeper into the stories you care about – powered by Metro and trusted publications.

Mikautadze will hope to show off his talents against the best team in Europe on Tuesday night when Villarreal take on Paris Saint-Germain.

PSG sit top of the group stage table with three wins from three games, looking very good in their bid to make it three Champions League titles on the spin.

Luis Enrique, the man who has led PSG to double European glory, has been philosophical on his achievements ahead of this encounter.

‘We have all won, we have all lost,’ he said. ‘I have been through countless situations where I was considered a “fraud” by a lot of people, and that fraud has kept evolving and improving, because that is the mindset a coach must have.

‘And now, everyone thinks I’m “the chosen one” or I don’t know what. And this is all a lie, all a lie.

‘The important thing is to follow your path. And along the path, the beautiful thing is that there are potholes, curves, and climbs.

‘Then the downhills also appear, which are very rewarding, but in the end, you appreciate the bad moments more. And if this is a “bad moment” for Villarreal, quote-unquote, I am sure they will get many positive things out of it.’

#1847. Coventry fan, 14, arrested following ‘cruel’ Bradley Lowery taunt in Sunderland match

A 14-year-old male has been arrested on suspicion of a public order offence and subsequently bailed after a video emerged appearing to show a Coventry fan taunting Sunderland supporters with a photograph of the late Bradley Lowery.

Bradley was a lifelong supporter of Sunderland and his battle with neuroblastoma, a rare form of childhood cancer, touched the hearts of supporters across the footballing world – and beyond – before his tragic death at the age of six in July 2017.

His legacy lives on through the Bradley Lowery Foundation which was established in August later that year and has helped support countless families in raising funds for treatment and equipment which is not readily available through the NHS.

Footage of the alleged incident came to light after Coventry’s 3-1 victory at home to Sunderland in the Premier League on Saturday afternoon.

Sign up to our daily football newsletter, pick your team and get the latest news sent directly to your inbox every morning.

The five-second clip in question appears to show a young spectator in the home end at the Coventry Building Society Arena grinning while pointing to a picture of Bradley on a mobile phone.

It is not the first time that Bradley’s story has seemingly been hijacked in such sickening circumstances, with Sheffield Wednesday fan Dale Houghton sacked from his job and handed a 12-month suspended prison sentence following a similar incident in 2023.

‘Coventry City FC is aware of footage circulating on social media in connection with an incident during our Premier League fixture against Sunderland,’ a statement from the Sky Blues read on Sunday.

Coventry City FC is aware of footage circulating on social media in connection with an incident during our Premier League fixture against Sunderland.The club does not tolerate offensive behaviour and will liaise with the relevant authorities to determine the appropriate course… pic.twitter.com/RxXnhtW3DF

‘The club does not tolerate offensive behaviour and will liaise with the relevant authorities to determine the appropriate course of action.’

It’s understood the teenage boy in question voluntarily handed himself into West Midlands Police, who, in turn, confirmed that an investigation was underway.

Use AI to go deeper into the stories you care about – powered by Metro and trusted publications.

The shocking video footage went viral on social media shortly after Coventry’s defeat of Sunderland and was widely condemned by both Black Cats fans and supporters of rival clubs.

A host of Coventry fans have also shown their support for Lowery’s family in the intervening days, with many leaving heartfelt messages alongside donations on JustGiving’s The Bradley Lowery Foundation fundraising page.

Lowery’s mother, Gemma, meanwhile, has called for her ‘beautiful boy’ to be ‘remembered with love, not hate’ in a heartbreaking statement on Instagram.

‘My beautiful boy deserves to be remembered with love, not hate. Yesterday, a Coventry fan used a photograph of Bradley to taunt Sunderland supporters,’ she wrote.

‘As Bradley’s mam, this is heartbreaking, especially as it’s one of my favourite photographs of him. Just look at that smile.

‘I remember that day like it was yesterday. He was so happy, having so much fun. Those moments were precious because they were few and far between. So much of Bradley’s short life was spent battling cancer and enduring treatments no child should ever face.

‘To see such a beautiful memory used in such a cruel way really does make my heart hurt.

‘We are a football-loving family who follow Sunderland home and away. I’m all for football banter, but surely mocking a child who died from cancer is not banter?

‘I hope the club takes appropriate action and the young lad’s family help him understand how hurtful his actions were. I don’t want hatred directed towards him, so please please don’t. I just for him to learn from this.

‘Behind that photograph is a little boy who was loved beyond measure and a family who miss him every day.’

To view this video please enable JavaScript, and consider upgrading to a web browser that supports HTML5 video

Gemma took the opportunity to thank those who had stepped up to defend Bradley since the video first began to circulate on social media.

‘Thank you to everyone who has defended Bradley and shown us so much love. It means more than you know,’ she added.

‘What some people don’t realise is that Bradley’s story didn’t end when his life did.

‘Because of Bradley, children’s lives are being saved, hundreds of families have received vital support, and children facing unimaginable battles are being given hope.

‘Through Super Brad’s Pad, families can escape hospital life, spend precious time together and make memories that last forever.‘That is Bradley’s legacy. The difference my little boy continues to make in this world. No amount of cruelty will ever take that away.‘So rather than let this photograph be remembered for hatred, I want it remembered for what it truly represents.

‘My beautiful little boy, enjoying one of the happiest days of his life, with the biggest smile on his face. That is how I want the world to remember him. #CancerHasNoColours Forever 6. Forever loved.’

Gemma finished by sharing a link to the Bradley Lowery Foundation’s website: www.bradleyloweryfoundation.com

#1846. Liverpool injury, suspension list and return dates for Fenerbahce: Hugo Ekitike, Jeremie Frimpong latest

By Lewis Nolan | 02 Nov 2026 03:25, Last updated: 02 Nov 2026 17:52

Liverpool must bounce back in the Champions League on Wednesday, when they take on Fenerbahce at Sukru Saracoglu Stadium.

Having lost 1-0 against Arsenal in the Premier League on Sunday, supporters are desperate for a confidence-boosting win.

The Reds have won all three Champions League games so far, but Andoni Iraola should be wary about underestimating Fenerbahce.

Here, Sports Mole rounds up Liverpool’s latest injury and suspension news ahead of their Champions League fixture against Fenerbahce.

Possible return date: November 22 (vs. Manchester United)

Speedster Jeremie Frimpong was brought on at half time against Brentford on October 17 but had to be replaced just seven minutes later with a hamstring injury.

The right-back is set to be sidelined until after the international break, and Iraola stated on October 19, "It’s going to be difficult, I think, before the [November international] break. We will try but it's going to be difficult to have him."

Possible return date: December 26 (vs. Hull City)

Striker Hugo Ekitike has been out of action since rupturing his Achilles against Paris Saint-Germain in April, and is going through rehabilitation following surgery on the tear.

The Frenchman is unlikely to take to the pitch for at least another couple of months, but has been included in Liverpool's squad for the Champions League league-phase, and could return during the festive period.

Possible return date: January 2 (vs. Coventry City)

Nineteen-year-old centre-back Giovanni Leoni is another long-term absentee for Liverpool, having suffered an anterior cruciate ligament injury on his debut in September 2025.

Speaking on October 15, Iraola revealed that the defender has faced a setback, saying, "It’s taking more time than we wanted. The plan was to train with the team in this past international break [but] probably it’s going to be in the next [one]."

Possible return date: November 22 (vs. Manchester United)

Right-back Conor Bradley has been unavailable since picking up a major knee injury against Arsenal in January, though he is planning a return this autumn.

The academy graduate has yet to join team training, but is making progress in his rehabilitation and started doing ball work earlier this month.

Liverpool have no players suspended for this match.

#1845. Jack Grealish can't turn down a good night out and his attitude is a problem. IAN HERBERT reveals how the magnetic maverick star sparked concern and now faces a tragedy of missed opportunity

By IAN HERBERT, DEPUTY CHIEF SPORTS WRITER

Published: 22:00 EDT, 29 October 2026 | Updated: 09:57 EDT, 2 November 2026

At the Pride of Britain awards a week back, we witnessed the brilliant and magnetic side of Jack Grealish, sprinkling stardust as he presented an award to a child of unimaginable courage who counts the Everton player as his hero. 'Footballers are classed as heroes – but these are the real heroes,' Grealish said that night. You could have heard a pin drop.

It was no different when he arrived back at Everton in September, to the delight of the kids awaiting him and his white Lamborghini in the country lane outside the club's Finch Farm training base. 'It feels so good. I think I'm at my best at everything in life when I feel loved,' Grealish said, articulating a very real sense that he was coming home.

He is popular around the club because it can be said without fear of exaggeration that he has a heart of gold.

Only on Thursday, an Everton-supporting father-of-three with a cancer diagnosis that gives him weeks to live disclosed that Grealish had put £10,000 his way. But within hours of that simple act of altruism coming to light, evidence of the other Grealish emerged, as Everton announced he had been excluded from the squad to face Newcastle in the Carabao Cup for failing to turn up for training last week.

It was by no means the first time. Everton sources say there had been similar causes for concern last season. Grealish reported sick ahead of last weekend's game at Arsenal, shortly after the Pride of Britain awards, and has breached Everton's disciplinary code through an unauthorised absence. The stated reason for his absence at Arsenal was illness.

Jack Grealish remains popular at Everton and has a heart of gold, shown by a £10,000 gift to a fan suffering from cancer, but he has since been dropped over a breach of discipline

There were similar causes for concern last season, with his return this summer going against David Moyes' better judgement

Everton's owners, looking for Grealish's glitz and glamour to gloss over their desperately poor and unambitious summer in the transfer window, were keen to bring him back. It was against David Moyes' own better judgement that he accepted his return as part of the deal that brought Iliman Ndiaye's unwelcome departure to Manchester City.

Moyes needed discipline in a thin squad where every player's contribution would count this season. It was an opportunity for the few star players to inspire and shine a light for the younger ones. And therein lies the tragedy of missed opportunity where Grealish is concerned.

He, the quintessential British maverick playmaker in the mould of George Best and Alan Hudson, could be a Goodison hero of these days, yet seems incapable of showing he is bothered, ridding himself of the acolytes and hangers on who are dragging him down, and appreciating what an opportunity football offers him.

Though he likes a drink, it's not so much booze as his attitude, and a struggle to turn down a good night out, which is contributing.

There is no doubt that he still has the skills to be a cherished player. That much was clear in the early stages of last season when he was providing more assists than any other Everton player until a broken foot requiring surgery brought a premature end to his season.

This season he has, as yet, no assists. He has perhaps been frustrated at the number of chances he has created not being converted, though not every winger has Erling Haaland as his support act.

Grealish's patchy attitude to a football life is affecting his game, as he is not taking his man on in the way he used to and does not emit such light on the wing

Look hard enough, though, and you'll see signs that his patchy attitude to a football life is affecting his game. He is not taking his man on in the way he used to and does not emit such light on the wing. Pep Guardiola, at Manchester City, was the first to see this and rapidly made it clear he wanted him gone.

It's not too late for the 31-year-old to become the totemic presence that so many fervently want him to be on Merseyside. Moyes, who sees the wasted potential, has given him abundant support and patience since City left him out in the cold, hoping that he can make him see the opportunity, here.

Thursday night's excellent Carabao Cup win over Newcastle United opens up the potential for an exciting Cup run, with Fleetwood Town awaiting in the quarter-finals. Everton have not won a trophy for 31 years.

The hope must be that the significantly public nature of Grealish's omission – very much a case of Moyes refusing to tolerate another breach – will shock him into action.

It was even the wish of Prime Minister Andy Burnham, present at Thursday night's match, that Grealish would be re-signed to Everton and the PM declared after meeting him at the Pride of Britain awards that the player was an example of the way people 'buy into Everton.'

The collective wish for him to thrive at the club could not be clearer. Only he can make that happen.

#1844. Goalkeeper Jesus Owono in ‘profound distress and anguish’ after death of Tenerife striker Jesus de Miguel

Andorra goalkeeper Jesus Owono ‘is experiencing profound distress and anguish’ after the death of Tenerife striker Jesus de Miguel.

De Miguel suffered head and chest injuries following a collision with Owono, who was sent off for his challenge near the halfway line, during the closing stages of the Spanish second-division match on Monday.

Owono had sprinted from his goal to clear a long ball when his knee collided with De Miguel’s chest.

De Miguel rolled on the floor immediately after impact but was then motionless on his back as several players urgently signalled for medical help.

Sign up to our daily football newsletter, pick your team and get the latest news sent directly to your inbox every morning.

The 30-year-old’s condition was first described as ‘stable, given the seriousness of the condition’ on Monday night but Tenerife issued a second update in the early hours of Tuesday morning which said that his ‘medical condition has deteriorated neurologically.’

Later on Tuesday morning, Tenerife announced that De Miguel had died in hospital.

Owono initially went to leave the pitch after his red card but then turned back after the severity of De Miguel’s situation became clear.

The 25-year-old, who was playing for La Liga side Alaves last year and has made 47 appearances for Equatorial Guinea’s national team, deleted his Instagram account after receiving abuse.

According to Spanish radio station COPE, some supporters at the Heliodoro Rodriguez Lopez stadium shouted ‘murderer’ at Owono, while the goalkeeper is said to have been crying and praying in the dressing room after the match was abandoned.

Use AI to go deeper into the stories you care about – powered by Metro and trusted publications.

Meanwhile, Venancio Tomas Ndong Micha, the president of the Equatorial Guinean Football Federation, has issued his ‘full solidarity and support’ to Owono.

‘It is with deep shock and immense sorrow that I have received the news of the tragic passing of your player, Jesus de Miguel. On behalf of the Equatorial Guinean Football Federation, and on my own behalf, I wish to express our most sincere and heartfelt condolences for this irreparable loss,’ Ndong Micha said in a statement.

‘Football is a family that, in moments like this, unites in grief. We wish to extend our deepest solidarity to his family, his teammates, the coaching staff, and all the blanquiazul (blue-and-white) fans, who are currently enduring a time of indescribable sadness.

‘Furthermore, I feel it is necessary to convey our full solidarity and support at this time to our player, Jesus Lazaro Owono.

‘We know that, as an involuntary participant in this fatal incident during the match, he is experiencing this situation with profound distress and anguish.

‘The Equatorial Guinean Football Federation offers him our full personal and professional support, fully aware of the severity of this event—something no one in our sport ever wishes to witness.

‘We share in your mourning and remain entirely at your disposal. Please accept our deepest respect and support during these most difficult times.’

On Tuesday, police in Spain opened an investigation for possible involuntary manslaughter following De Miguel’s death.

Judicial authorities in the Canary Islands said it is a routine procedure as any death deemed non-natural under Spanish law automatically triggers a judicial inquiry.

However, the chief prosecutor of Santa Cruz de Tenerife, Jose Luis Sanchez-Jauregui, has said it would be ‘very difficult’ for a criminal process to be opened as De Miguel’s collision with Owono occurred during the match.

Speaking to Spanish news agency EFE, Sanchez-Jauregui explained that long-standing Spanish Supreme Court precedent distinguishes injuries sustained during a match from deliberate assaults which are committed when play is halted.

Sanchez-Jauregui added that the referee’s report and the decision of the Sports Disciplinary Committee, which will determine whether Owono intended to cause harm with his challenge on De Miguel, will be considered before any legal action.

On Tuesday afternoon, the Royal Spanish Football Federation (RFEF) announced that all of its football competitions have been suspended until November 6.

#1843. Alexander Isak starts to justify £125m price tag with double

There was a centre-forward who played for Newcastle a couple of years ago. Do you remember him? He was as quick as greased lightning, played on his instincts, had a shot like cannon and could come up with a finish for every situation.

Everyone wanted him, but Liverpool signed him for £125m in August 2025. His name was Alexander Isak but shortly after arriving on Merseyside, it was like he went missing, as the guy who played in red last season bore only a physical resemblance to the guy who had played in black-and-white.

If you had wondered what had happened to him, he reappeared at Portman Road. They say good things come to those who wait. Although nobody at Liverpool would have expected such a delay to see the real Isak, there were no complaints that his career at the club has finally taken off.

Taking the headlines from Bradley Barcola on a big night at Portman Road was going to take some doing, but Isak did just that with a double salvo in the opening nine minutes, a flurry so potent it was like a boxer charging out of their corner and seeing the first blows land flush on their opponent’s jaw.

Poor Ipswich. There is universal recognition that Liverpool are a team – and a club – in transition but they had four players in Isak, Florian Wirtz, Cody Gakpo and Victor Muñoz who had the potential to dismantle the hosts if they clicked and that is precisely what happened.

“With Alex, it is clear,” said Andoni Iraola. “If he is fit, if he is available, if he is in a good shape, he will produce the numbers. My demand with Alex will not be about the goals. It will be about other things so we can play well. And if we play well, we are in good positions. Then goals will come.”

So for all the noisy backing they received from the stands and for all the effort Gary O’Neil’s side put into a contest that TV companies had chosen to broadcast because there was a potential for drama, Isak blew a hole in Ipswich’s hull in the sixth minute and they were submerging from there on in.

A blistering finish from Alexander Isak! 💥 pic.twitter.com/jSGlIZsQtA

How Isak, who had scored against Nottingham Forest last weekend, needed a night like this when he made a genuine difference. But the same was true, too, for Iraola. We live in an era where someone has to be in the eye of a storm and the Basque will know what comes with his new territory.

It had clearly irritated Iraola that Liverpool had gone behind four times in their opening two fixtures and during his pre-match media briefing, he effectively gave a sermon at one point on how slow starts, or giving the opposition a helping hand, would no longer be tolerated.

Quietly, Iraola is making his presence felt. The task he faces is significantly different than the one O’Neil is accomplishing – keeping Ipswich in the division against the odds – but Liverpool’s head coach is a man who knows his own mind and is not afraid to make decisions.

He had responded to criticism of his midfield at Newcastle on the opening weekend by dropping Ryan Gravenberch for the fixture with Forest and his response to scrutiny about his right-back seven days ago was to drop Jeremie Frimpong and bring in Ronald Araújo.

Iraola certainly picked the right team: Araújo, the loan capture from Barcelona, added stature to the back four and there was harmony in how they moved. The Uruguayan’s first instinct was to stay back and Liverpool looked better for it, even if O’Neil, incredibly, felt Ipswich had the better of things.

Emersonn, Ipswich’s Brazilian striker, did not see the ball in the opening exchanges and, by the time he did, Liverpool had zoomed into the distance to such an extent that you felt it was going to be impossible for them to peg their visitors back.

“I hate having to talk about good performances when you do not get points,” O’Neil declared to a room full of raised eyebrows and you can only assume his message was to ensure that morale in the dressing room was not drooping.

What damage was inflicted with Liverpool’s first significant attack. Gakpo, the subject of an £80m bid from Manchester City, was never going to allow transfer speculation to disrupt his focus and he nudged a perfect little ball into Isak’s path in the sixth minute to show his wellbeing.

The next move announced the return of Isak. One touch gave him an avenue to shoot, the next was a shot with his right foot that was so hard from 16 yards, on an angle, it bent the wrists of Kjell Scherpen as it howled into the net. Critics will feel Ipswich’s keeper should have done better.

Your first thought was to think of the first goal Isak scored in English football in September 2022, a similarly venomous drive, against Liverpool at Anfield. He oozed quality that evening, his pace and skill had Jürgen Klopp’s defenders persistently fretting and this is what he was doing again.

It was no coincidence that three minutes later, he came up with another wonderful goal. This one owed much to the beautiful pass Gakpo presented to him, an inch-perfect through ball with the outside of his right foot, but Isak still showed great poise to bamboozle Scherpen.

Inside NINE minutes Alexander Isak has two goals! ⚡️ pic.twitter.com/3UGq0bwqRm

“He owes me a few assists now!” chirped the selfless Gakpo.

A hat-trick could have arrived in the 32nd minute but Isak was a kneecap offside as he dispatched a pass from Wirtz and, perhaps, he will have been disappointed to have made way on the hour having not secured the match ball for his efforts.

Liverpool, too, will be frustrated that they did not made sure of three points before the time Isak made way for Barcola – what Alexis Mac Alliser was thinking when he fluffed an unmarked header from six yards, only he will know – but it was not a night to nitpick.

There will be easier assignments on the horizon for Ipswich, even though O’Neil insisted they more than held their own against world-class opponents. And you can say for sure there will be more goals and wins for Liverpool and Isak if they continue in this encouraging manner.

“I witnessed what a great coach he was at Bournemouth. He is not the sort of manager you are going to see making clever patterns in his box. He just does not see the risk. He will want to get the ball to the players who want to make a difference. Coaches do not show how good they are by how they play out from the back. The important thing is when you get it in the final third, you make things happen. That is what he will want to improve. He will want Alexander Isak when he has not got the ball to press. He will want the same of Florian Wirtz. The difficulty will come with Champions League football and not putting too many demands on his players. If he gets it right, he has got a wonderful squad to work with.”

"My demands will not be about the goals, my fights with him are about other stuff." Andoni Iraola speaking about Alexander Isak 🔊 pic.twitter.com/B4zUG2IGfS

“He has had good minutes, a good pass in a counter, a good couple of chances when he was going against the goalkeeper and we have not found him. We need to learn these movements because he will be there threatening in behind all the team. But he looks confident on the ball as always. He had not played any competitive minutes since the World Cup so we had to be a little bit more careful.”

"Yeah, that's nice" 😁Alexander Isak talks through his second goal vs Ipswich 🔍 pic.twitter.com/diG2xv50Bw

“We were waiting for the first win, and we were talking about starting the game well, which we have not done recently. And we did that with two goals. With a normal pre-season, I think we are starting to get the way we want to play, being offensive and attack the defence. We showed that today. We scored two and could have scored more.

“It was not easy. It was a long injury, a difficult season [last season] in general. I was thinking; I want to have a good World Cup firstly and then to start the season well, which I feel like I have done now. That season is kind of behind me, but it was not easy.”

The final whistle goes at Portman Road and Andoni Iraola picks up his first win as Liverpool boss with a 2-0 victory thanks to Isak’s quickfire double inside the opening 10 minutes. Like they did two seasons ago, Liverpool win 2-0 at Portman Road.

Kerkez is the latest player into the book for a foul on Fatawu.

Fatawu receives it out on the right for Ipswich and cuts inside onto his preferred left foot before curling an effort towards the far post but it goes wide.

Jacquet takes a heavy touch from a high ball and ends up taking out Emersonn, which earns the Frenchman a booking.

Liverpool work it well down their left as Isak plays it into Gakpo, who drives towards the Ipswich box. He plays it across the face of the penalty area to Szboszblai, who flicks it first time into the path of Wirtz. The German’s effort takes a deflection and goes behind for a corner.

Szoboszlai’s outswinger finds a free Mac Allister at the front post but the Argentine’s header is straight at Scherpen. That was a good chance for Mac Allister.

We are back under way at Portman Road. No changes for either side at the break.

We have just seen replays of a possible penalty shout for Liverpool right at the end of the first half for a foul on Gakpo by Fatawu and it looked a decent shout.

Possession: Ipswich 41%-59% LiverpoolShots: 8-7Shots on target: 2-6Corners: 3-2Touches in opposition box: 7-12

Perhaps if Liverpool were playing a team with a bit more savvy, the 2-0 scoreline they currently protect would have been in jeopardy. Ipswich have put some nice moves together and had half chances but not enough to really turn the screw. Andoni Iraola, certainly, has been unhappy at times and it is becoming a trademark to see him spin around from the technical area in disgust when a ball has been squandered. In the main, though, he can be satisfied with this opening 45 minutes. Liverpool should be winning from here.

The first half is brought to an end at Portman Road and Isak’s quickfire double early in the half gives Liverpool a 2-0 lead at the break.

Wirtz feeds a lovely pass into the left channel to pick out the run of Isak into the Ipswich box but Diop comes in with a crucial challenge.

Two added minutes at the end of this first half.

Araujo slices a clearance out of play for an Ipswich corner. A real gift for the home side as Araujo was not under any real pressure.

Isak should head away at the near post but it comes to Mac Allister to clear away.

A chance for Wirtz as the ball falls to the German on the edge of the Ipswich box but his shot is saved by Scherpen down to his left.

Enciso is the first Ipswich player into the book tonight for delaying a restart.

Szoboszlai, for the third time in the half, shoots from range. Again, the Hungarian gets plenty of power on it but fortunately for Scherpen it is straight at him.

Enciso turns neatly not far outside the Liverpool box and then shoots but slices the shot a fair way wide.

Tommy Elphick, a member of Andoni Iraola’s coaching staff, is booked for his protestations. Liverpool are not happy with some of the fouls being given against them and then some that are not given for them, including a clear foul from Emersonn on Van Dijk that was not penalised.

Isak has the ball in the Ipswich net for the third time tonight and thinks he has his hat-trick but the offside flag goes up. It comes from a stunning piece of play from Wirtz down Liverpool’s left, taking up a pocket of space and taking the ball on the turn beautifully. He then spots Isak in space at the far post and picks him out perfectly, with Isak slotting home. However, the offside flag is up and replays prove he was just offside. Could Isak have timed his run just fractionally better and still reached the cross? Probably but it was very close.

Mac Allister receives a pass from Wirtz and, from just outside the box, decides to shoot but his effort goes just over. Scherpen did appear to have it covered anyway.

A crucial intervention from Araujo. Enciso drives down Ipswich’s right after Fatawu’s header, with Mac Allister tracking back. From the right side of the Liverpool box, Enciso’s deflected cross comes towards Maeda at the far post but Araujo makes an important clearance.

Moments later, Davis again meets a Fatawu cross at the far post but his header is off target.

Fatawu’s dangerous cross from the right all the way to the back post finds Davis, who heads back across goal. Emersonn takes a touch with his chest on the edge of the six-yard box before shooting but Jacquet is on hand to make a crucial block. Ipswich though do have their first corner of the game.

Lukic clips it in and Alisson should punch away with ease. However, the ball comes off Gakpo and, very fortunately for Alisson, the ball gets trapped between his own legs and he can gather. Alisson will be a relieved man.

Szoboszlai sends another powerful shot from range towards the goal and forces Scherpen into another decent save. Ipswich are not helping themselves at times by just giving the ball away inside their own half.

Szoboszlai comes close to adding a third for Liverpool. Fatawu inexplicably gives the ball away inside his own half before Mac Allister plays it forward to Szoboszlai, who takes just one touch before firing towards goal. Scherpen gets down well to his right to make the save.

And there he is. You have been waiting 12 months to see the Alexander Isak of Newcastle play for Liverpool but here he is, a confident, instinctive-finishing menace. His first goal was marvellous, his second was a work of art, given the pass from Cody Gakpo, and what a position Liverpool have put themselves in to get their first win under Andoni Iraola. And, while we are at it, Gakpo has made both Liverpool’s goals: what on earth were they doing thinking of selling him to Manchester City?

Isak, on his last trip to Portman Road, scored a hat-trick for Newcastle here in a 4-0 win back in December 2024. He already has two goals to his name tonight inside the opening quarter of an hour.

Emersonn misses from close range for Ipswich but the offside flag goes up against Greaves. It was a bad miss from Emersonn but Greaves, who had delivered the cross for Emersonn, was offside.

The first booking of the game goes the way of Mac Allister, who is booked slightly harshly for a foul on Enciso.

Moments later, Ipswich have their first effort of the game but Fatawu curls over from the edge of the box.

Another fine goal from Isak and Liverpool lead 2-0 not even 10 minutes into this game. It is Gakpo who assists again with a superb pass with the outside of his right foot from halfway into the left channel to pick out the run in behind of Isak. The Swede cuts inside Greaves onto his right before then chopping back onto his left. He then coolly slots home past Scherpen and Liverpool have the dream start.

Inside NINE minutes Alexander Isak has two goals! ⚡️ pic.twitter.com/3UGq0bwqRm

Liverpool take a deserved lead at Portman Road. Kerkez wins the ball back for Liverpool on halfway and the ball comes to Gakpo. The Dutchman drives forward and spots Isak in space to his right. Isak’s movement is very clever as he drifts off the defender into space. He takes a touch before smashing the ball past Scherpen at his near post. Should Scherpen have saved that? Possibly but Isak did hit that very hard. For the first time this season, Liverpool lead in a Premier League match.

A blistering finish from Alexander Isak! 💥 pic.twitter.com/jSGlIZsQtA

Wirtz is penalised for a very soft foul on Enciso, who just threw his hands in the air after the slightest bits of contact. The referee Darren England was not initially going to give it but eventually does, giving Ipswich the chance to swing it in from the left into the Liverpool penalty area.

Fatawu swings it in with his left but Alisson punches away.

It has been all Liverpool in these early stages but have yet to have a shot. Ipswich have barely touched the ball thus far.

Liverpool win the first corner of the game as Davis is forced to put it behind after good work from Munoz down Liverpool’s right.

Szoboszlai’s outswinger is headed away from danger.

Both sides emerge from the tunnel at Portman Road and we are moments away from kick-off. Here is a reminder of how the two sides line up this evening:

Ipswich: Scherpen, O’Shea, Diop, Greaves, Davis, Palacios, Lukic, Fatawu, Enciso, Maeda, Emersonn.Substitutes: Walton, Furlong, Kipre, Ouattara, Florentino, Nunez, McAteer, Clarke, Flemming.

Liverpool: Alisson; Jacquet, Araujo, Van Dijk, Kerkez; Mac Allister, Szoboszlai, Wirtz; Munoz, Isak, Gakpo.Substitutes: Mamardashvili, Endo, Tsimikas, Barcola, Frimpong, Gravenberch, Nyoni, Koumas, Ngumoha.

"Everyone's going to love him" 😍Jamie Redknapp is looking forward to seeing Bradley Barcola play for Liverpool this evening! pic.twitter.com/Ut9Zx4gbB2

The Paraguayan is in his second stint at Ipswich and has two assists to his name in the first two league games.

"He is the talisman already inside these first two games"Can Julio Enciso provide another assist tonight? 👀 pic.twitter.com/FaDkndt3BG

"I'm desperate for him to do well!" Jamie Redknapp says Florian Wirtz has to produce more for Liverpool right now 💭 pic.twitter.com/1fYT9t9tx3

A milestone appearance for Dom 🫰🔴 pic.twitter.com/C28iemsxou

"I really feel they've got that recruitment right' Luke Chambers says the Premier League experience of players that Ipswich have signed will be massive for them 🧠 pic.twitter.com/DgwYsTlHBD

“It gives us a big belief that we can compete at the level. Coming up from the Championship, there is always some doubt around. The home win over Sunderland was huge for us. And then to be in the game for as long as we were at Manchester United was impressive. I have challenged the lads a lot. We do not focus on the outcome or results, we just commit to being the best version of ourselves. We cannot go toe-to-toe with everyone. We have to be sensible and smart.”

Andoni Iraola has made a change at right-back tonight, with Ronaldu Araujo replacing Jeremie Frimpong. Araujo arrived at Liverpool this summer on loan with an option to buy from Barcelona.

A first Reds start for Ronald 💪 pic.twitter.com/P80pwhlBJ9

"He's ready, definitely we will use him in the second half" Andoni Iraola says Bradley Barcola has looked good in training and is hoping to give him some game time against Ipswich ⏳ pic.twitter.com/C00WVI7ACd

Andoni Iraola wondered what might happen when he first sat down to talk with Bradley Barcola.

Here was one of the world’s best wingers, with his 13 major honours, 28 international caps and £123m price tag – a combination that could easily lead a man to view himself through the prism of a superstar: never mind what I can do for you, what can you do for me?

Liverpool’s due diligence on Barcola had all been positive – not least from the currently injured Hugo Ekitike, who had been a vocal advocate of his compatriot’s capabilities to the recruitment team – but Iraola wanted to gauge for himself exactly what the 24-year-old was going to offer.

Ipswich were very active in the market upon their return to the Premier League, making 14 signings in total, with plenty of them involved tonight. Here is a sample of what Gary O’Neil’s side did during the window:

We are about to find out the two starting XIs at Portman Road. Will Bradley Barcola start for Liverpool on his debut?

The third matchday of the new Premier League season kicks off at Portman Road as newly-promoted Ipswich host Liverpool.

Andoni Iraola has drawn his first two games in charge of Liverpool, both 2-2 stalemates against Newcastle and Nottingham Forest respectively. Liverpool secured a move for forward Bradley Barcola from PSG in the final few days on the window for a fee that could rise to £123m and the Frenchman is set to make his Liverpool debut tonight.

“We are very happy with Bradley,” Iraola said. “He was our priority; to sign a very good player in that position. He has come with the right mentality. I like that he wanted Liverpool a lot, he just wanted to come here. That is a good first sign. Being the player he is and the things he has won recently, he has come with the willingness to help us. I am very happy with him.

“He trained well with us, and if everything goes well in today’s [Thursday] training, he will definitely be available for tomorrow [tonight]. He has trained with us three times. He has not had minutes in pre-season but he has been training normally with the group. It is a decision we have to make. We have to consider that he has not had minutes in pre-season.”

Liverpool won both fixtures when Ipswich were last in the Premier League two seasons ago, including a 2-0 win on the opening weekend in Arne Slot’s first game in charge of Liverpool as they went on to win the Premier League that season.

Ipswich won their first home game on their return to the Premier League, beating Sunderland 2-1 on the opening weekend. However, they fell to a 5-2 defeat in their first away game at Manchester United. Over the course of the summer transfer window, Ipswich made a total of 14 signings and spent over £200m.

“What we can do is perform in a way that always gives us a real chance, which we have done so far,” Ipswich boss Gary O’Neil said. “We were in that game at Manchester United until a couple of moments took it away from us. We were in it, so that is what we need to do, we need to make sure that no matter who it is, whether it is Liverpool, Manchester United, Manchester City, when they come to Portman Road, we need to make sure we are right in the game to give ourselves opportunities. We will always be a threat; we have scored four goals in two games. That is really good for a promoted side. We look a goal threat, and we need to keep that going and that will be tested.”

Team news from Portman Road to follow shortly.

#1842. Kaka discusses Hall of Fame induction, tonight’s derby and the Milan project

AC Milan legend Ricky Kaka will be inducted into the Rossoneri’s Hall of Fame ahead of tonight’s derby, which he believes is anyone’s game.

As confirmed in the last few days, after inducting the likes of Marco van Basten, Filippo Inzaghi, Andriy Shevchenko and more, it’s now time for Kaka. The Brazilian is one of the greatest players to have even worn the red and black shirt, scoring 104 goals and assisting another 81 in  307 games.

Read SempreMilan ad-free and get access to exclusive news. Click here for a free trial!

The ceremony will take place before tonight’s derby clash between AC Milan and Inter, which is a very important game for the Rossoneri. A loss would leave them 10 points behind the top, so hopefully Kaka’s presence and celebration can act as fuel for the team.

Speaking to Gazzetta dello Sport, Kaka shared his thoughts on the Hall of Fame, his memories of the derby and what will be needed from Milan tonight. He also commented on the Rossoneri’s project as a whole, stating that time is needed.

“I’m getting ready. My family will be there. My wife, daughters, my brother, and many friends. I also wanted to thank the fans who voted. I can imagine the atmosphere. It’ll be exciting.”

What do you remember about your first derby?

“A header from a cross by Rino Gattuso. It was also my first goal for AC Milan. Fantastic. The city experiences this match in a special way; among my memories, I’d logically put the Champions League derby in the quarterfinals. The comeback from 3-2 was also fantastic.”

You mentioned Gattuso, who as a coach, after changing many clubs, is doing well with Lazio…

“Being a coach is a tough job. Rino is doing really well now. He has a very special character, he’s someone who always wants to win, and I’m happy he’s able to express himself to the fullest. He’s a great friend, I always cheer for my friends and I’m very happy.”

“Let’s say no, for now. The pressure of the coaching job isn’t for me. But we can talk about it again in a couple of years.”

Speaking of friends, what do you think of the Paolo Maldini and Leonardo affair with the national team?

“I’m amazed at how little time passed before their resignations. It’s difficult to judge from afar, but I think it would have been a good thing for Italian football to have such competent people at the helm. I hope Italy regains its place soon.

“There are so many things to manage, from youth development onwards. I often meet with former players who live in Italy and ask questions. Italy at the World Cup is a good thing for football as a whole.

“Plus, my connection to Italy is incredibly strong; I try to return at least once a year, and more if I can. In recent years, we’ve visited the art cities, Florence, Venice, but also the lakes, Capri, and the sea. And Sardinia is wonderful.”

Let’s get back to football. Were you surprised by Milan’s collapse last season?

“I think all the fans expected us to qualify for the Champions League. Was it a physical or mental decline? Maybe a bit of everything. When confidence starts to wane, everything changes. Now, however, we must aim to return to the best of Europe. The Champions League is special.”

“It’s under construction. For seven years, it was Leao’s Milan, a great player on whom a lot of trust was placed. Now it’s different. The team is a collective with new faces and two masters: Modric remains the brains, then there’s Rabiot. And Ramos is a goalscorer.

“It will take some time to put it together. The important thing is to always aim high, even in the Europa League.”

What kind of relationship did you have with the Inter fans?

“A relationship of great respect. Inter helped me grow a lot because I’ve always looked at competition as something that helps me grow, so I saw the matches against Inter or Juventus as important matches, and I had to prepare well because the team was very strong, the opponents were very strong.

“But with the Brazilians of my time, Maicon, Julio, and the others, there was friendship. And also with the Argentines: many others were and remain friends, like Materazzi.”

How do you see Inter on this evening, which will be special for you?

“They are still doing well after last season. They’re a team to beat, but we Milan fans can do it already in this derby. Chivu as a coach was a nice surprise; Inter didn’t play well at the start, but then they corrected their position. But I wouldn’t say the Scudetto is a one-man showdown like you might think in Italy.

“I see the game as open and the road to the title even more so. The season is long, but Milan must aim to be consistent. So far they’ve done better in the league than in Europe, there will be moments of decline in the other teams and we’ll have to take advantage of them.”

“Not great at the World Cup, but it takes a bit of time. The national team is different from a club where you’re there every day evaluating players. Carlo was only able to work with the group for a year.

“For the next World Cup, it will be five years of preparation, five years with these guys, learning the culture of the country, knowing a little about what it’s like to play in the World Cup with Brazil. So I have a lot of confidence.”

You won the Ballon d’Or in 2007 and no one had any reason to argue. This time they gave it to Harry Kane, and Lamine Yamal doesn’t seem to have taken it too well. Your opinion?

“The right choice. Harry Kane has done very well, he was a key player with Bayern Munich and won a lot. Mbappé didn’t win much with Real Madrid, Lamine had success with Barça but wasn’t as decisive as expected. Their time will come, but I think the choice based on their performance this season is acceptable.”

Let’s get back to the derby. Who are the key players?

“Modric and Rabiot are masters, they manage and set the pace. Pulisic enchants me with his intelligence in the game, Goncalo is a goalscorer. As for Inter, what can I say? They are a consistent, solid team and have many dangerous players.”

Do you have any favourite places in Milan?

“I like walking downtown, I like Brera, I love the hidden corners. Drinking coffee, talking to people.”

#1841. Liverpool 0-1 Arsenal: What went wrong for Andoni Iraola's Reds as Mikel Arteta's Gunners claim Anfield Premier League win

By Anthony Nolan | 02 Nov 2026 05:17

Liverpool were downed 1-0 by Arsenal in a tense showdown at Anfield on Sunday, with the Gunners claiming a first Premier League victory at the iconic ground in 14 years.

Andoni Iraola's side were arguably the better team on the day, but they proved unable to fashion much in the way of clear-cut chances, owing to struggles in buildup and the visitors' extremely defensive playstyle.

The Merseysiders were unfortunate to not be awarded a penalty in the first half, when Alexander Isak was pulled back by Jurrien Timber, and it has been said that Liverpool were punished for being 'too honest' at the weekend.

Another decisive factor in the defeat was the manner in which the Reds lost their momentum and grip on the contest following the introduction of Dominik Szoboszlai in the second half.

Here, Sports Mole takes a closer look at what went wrong for Iraola during Liverpool's loss to Arsenal on Sunday.

It is no secret that Trent Alexander-Arnold's departure to Real Madrid in the summer of 2025 was a major blow for Liverpool, and his absence is still keenly felt on Merseyside.

The right-back was key to the Reds' buildup from deep areas under Jurgen Klopp and during the title-winning 2024-25 campaign with Arne Slot at the helm, but the club are yet to sign a capable replacement.

Ronald Araujo has been exceptional on the right of Iraola's defence in the early stages of this term, though the Uruguayan is by no means a strong passer or progressor of the ball, considering that he is a natural centre-back.

On the opposite flank, left-back Milos Kerkez has been capable when defending but lacklustre going forward - the inverse of fans' concerns when he arrived at Anfield from Bournemouth.

Thanks to a lack of attacking influence from their full-backs, Liverpool have struggled to move the ball from deep areas at pace or with fluidity, a weakness in the team that has encouraged opposition presses.

On Sunday, the Reds conceded the decisive goal after a misplaced pass from Alisson while playing out from the back, and saw a number of counter-attacking opportunities break down when centre-backs Virgil van Dijk and Jeremy Jacquet were not available to initiate them.

For reference, Araujo completed one pass into the final third and Kerkez three, while Jacquet made six and Van Dijk nine, highlighting just how little impact Iraola's wide defenders are having on the attack.

"I think it was also a clear penalty" "Doesn't notice it? We have 50 cameras." A disappointed Virgil van Dijk shares his thoughts on the Alexander Isak penalty shout ? pic.twitter.com/XgruCrTjT6

Arsenal are recognised throughout the Premier League as a team that play to the margins of the rules, while Liverpool were on the receiving end of a number of controversial decisions on Sunday.

The most notable incident occurred part way through the first half, when Isak came close to heading a Bradley Barcola cross goalwards, only for Timber to clearly pull the striker's jersey and impede his movement towards the ball.

Neither referee Andy Madley nor VAR intervened on that occasion, supposedly missing the pull entirely, with commentators and pundits alike putting blame on Isak for not throwing himself to the ground for attention as Arsenal stars such as Gabriel had done to great effect at Anfield.

After the loss, Iraola was asked whether it was necessary to instruct players to go to ground, with the manager saying, "It's a shame you ask me this question. But honestly, yes, we have to tell them to go down because they are not going to call it otherwise."

Liverpool captain Van Dijk was also frustrated with the failure to spot the pull, telling the media, "We have 50 cameras. Why does [Isak] have to complain when there are so many cameras? Everyone has seen it. In the end it wasn't given and we lose the game unfortunately, so well done to Arsenal."

The other flashpoint in the match was the head-to-head between Noni Madueke and Alexis Mac Allister, during which the Argentine midfielder made sure to excessively exaggerate his reaction to the Arsenal winger's aggression.

VAR decided that Madueke's head movement did not meet the standards for violent conduct, but it came as a surprise that he avoided a yellow card, especially considering that the Englishman had already been booked earlier in the half for stopping a counter.

Back in April this year, Gabriel appeared to headbutt Manchester City's Erling Haaland, but when the striker failed to dive, the Gunners defender escaped a red card and both players were shown a yellow for displaying aggressive behaviour.

The inconsistency in punishment between incidents of a similar nature is frustrating for everyone invested in the game, though there does appear to be a 'correct' amount of exaggeration that will attract a referee's attention without arousing suspicion, and Arsenal have mastered the art of it.

Iraola's side have been without Dominik Szoboszlai for five of the past six games due to the minor hamstring issue that forced him to be withdrawn against Brentford on October 17.

The number eight came off the bench on Sunday with the Reds searching for a goal, but the team appeared to lose fluency in midfield following his introduction.

Nineteen-year-old Trey Nyoni, who Szoboszlai replaced, had kept Liverpool on the front foot by completing 78% of his a progressive passes, 67% of his long passes and 96% of his passes overall.

By contrast, the Hungary captain proved wasteful in possession once again, with just 30% of his progressive passes reaching their destination, as well as 29% of his long balls and 82% of his passes as a whole.

Szoboszlai is not a natural fit in a deeper midfield role, and he lacks the close control or consistency to feature in the number 10 position, though his unique running power makes it difficult for Iraola to leave him out of the XI.

Similarly, Ryan Gravenberch seems to have been displaced in the pecking order by Nyoni, given the former Bayern Munich and Ajax star did not see a single minute against Arsenal and has now started just four of the Reds' nine Premier League games this term.

The Dutchman is often seen as an important player for Liverpool by many due to the fact he claimed the Young Player of the Season award in 2024-25, but the reality is that he has struggled beyond the initial months of Slot's tenure.

Gravenberch also failed to establish himself during Klopp's final campaign at the club, and the 24-year-old faces an uncertain future at Anfield, despite the six-year contract he penned in March this year that may become something of an albatross for the Reds.

#1840. Wayne Rooney slams Bruno Fernandes during Manchester United’s comeback win over Roma

Wayne Rooney criticised Bruno Fernandes for not running back during Manchester United’s remarkable comeback win over Roma in the Champions League.

United, enduring their worst start to a season since the 1980s, looked on course for their fifth defeat in six games as they trailed Roma 2-0 at Old Trafford.

Michael Carrick once again called on his players to produce an improved performance following a shocking run but the Red Devils fell behind inside 12 minutes.

The Serie A side took advantage of the acres of space left on the left-hand side by the out-of-position Diogo Dalot to take the lead through Matias Soule.

Sign up to our daily football newsletter, pick your team and get the latest news sent directly to your inbox every morning.

A similar gap in the Manchester United defence led to Roma’s second as Ayden Heaven was penalised for a handball blocking a shot and Donyell Malen converted from the penalty spot.

Dalot attracted much criticism for his part in Roma’s goals but Rooney was disappointed by Fernandes’ lack of effort in getting back, especially given his status as club captain.

It looked as though Fernandes’ woes would deepen when he missed a second-half penalty but he was offered a reprieve due to encroachment and tucked his second effort away.

The goal, scored just before the hour mark, lifted Old Trafford but Manchester United still trailed with 10 minutes remaining.

In an extraordinary comeback that may have saved Carrick his job, Matheus Cunha then scored two goals in the space of three minutes to completely turn the game on its head.

Use AI to go deeper into the stories you care about – powered by Metro and trusted publications.

Cunha was shown a yellow card for jumping into the stands during his goal celebrations and received another shortly after, but United were still able to hold on with ten men to clinch a remarkable and unlikely victory.

Speaking on Amazon Prime at half-time, Rooney said the team were ‘shot to bits’ and was shocked by a lacklustre first-half display.

Asked whether the opening 45 minutes felt like a ‘new low’ for his former club, Rooney said: ‘Yeah, there’s been a lot of those lately but yeah, it did.

‘You’re in the Champions League and with all the talk and criticism the team have got, you were expecting some sort of reaction. There was nothing, absolutely nothing.

THAT DIDN'T TAKE LONG 😬United fall behind after just 11 minutes as Roma score through Matías Soulé 🇦🇷 pic.twitter.com/DtIOFJYZ6D

‘Roma took the ball and were more aggressive, no one on the United team put a tackle in. They were really struggling down the left-hand side.

‘You just want to see something, some sort of fight and passion and desire to win the football game but there was nothing.

‘For the first goal, if you’re playing in a system, when Dalot goes higher, Bruno should go into that position. He has to run back, you’re the captain of the football club, run back and take responsibility.

‘You’re a team and you need to play as a team. If a teammate is out of position, even if you don’t want to be there or run back, you have to run back.

‘I feel so sorry for the fans because they don’t know what to do. They’ve not been in this position for years, they don’t know whether to get behind the team or to get on their backs. I feel so sorry for them.

‘The team have just run out of ideas. There’s no confidence or belief, the team is shot to bits.’

Reacting to Manchester United’s comeback win after full-time, Rooney added: ‘The second-half was amazing, they were front-footed and they deserved to win the game in the end.

‘The first half was terrible but we saw the passion and fight we wanted in the second half. The crowd got right behind the team and you felt like they could go on to win the game.’

Fellow England legend Alan Shearer, meanwhile, said: ‘Great credit to Michael Carrick because they were down and out at half-time.

‘They were all over the place in that first-half, and he had to change and tweak things.

‘I said what can he do, I didn’t know where he would start, and he must have started in the dressing room, and pointing at a few people telling them to be brave and courageous and move the ball quicker.

‘They did all those things in the second half and got their reward by getting their win.’

Manchester United, sitting just 17th in the Premier League, face Unai Emery’s Aston Villa at Old Trafford this weekend.

#1839. Harry Kane explains how his versatility could be the future of football

By Axel Clody | 02 Nov 2026 06:45, Last updated: 02 Nov 2026 06:46

Harry Kane’s Ballon d’Or is a recognition of far more than a goalscorer. The Bayern Munich and England striker will, of course, be remembered for his 73 goals last season, but even more for his ability to operate outside the box almost like a playmaker.

Even defensively the centre-forward caught the eye, especially in a clash with Borussia Dortmund last October, when he dropped back into midfield and defended in front of the box with sliding tackles.

In a lengthy interview with France Football magazine, which is responsible for the award for the best player in the world, published this weekend, the 33-year-old was asked what story his triumph would tell. He highlighted precisely his characteristics.

‘People have really started to see the whole package of my game: my passing, my dropping deep to get the ball, creating space for team-mates, my defending, tracking back to help the team and contributing in different ways. As a No. 9, I do not think there are many strikers capable of playing in so many different positions’ - Kane said.

Kane revealed that his quality away from the box can be explained by his experience in midfield and defence as a youngster. ‘That helped me learn to play in different positions.’ The Bayern forward sees this kind of multi-skilled player, capable of playing in different roles, as the future of the sport.

‘One day we might play with systems where players do not really have fixed positions. They will simply be on the pitch, able to adapt to every situation. Maybe that is how football should be played, with intelligence and a good understanding of the game. I just need to keep showing all my qualities at the highest level. The future will tell how I will be regarded’ - Kane said.

Kane’s award is also a message to those who see football only through dribbles and a subjective ‘magic’.

The Englishman was competing for the prize with Kylian Mbappe and Lamine Yamal, who finished second and third respectively in the 2026 Ballon d’Or. Both have a more eye-catching style, with a repertoire of dribbles, especially the young Spaniard.

The centre-forward is proud that his ‘quiet’ style has been rewarded, which reveals an unexpected way for the France Football voters to assess the candidates. The voters were 100 journalists from the 100 highest-ranked countries in FIFA’s national team rankings.

‘I know the Ballon d’Or sometimes rewards the player who has something special, the one who can decide a match with a dribble, with his speed or with a spectacular move. But that is also what makes this Ballon d’Or so special in my eyes: I have the feeling that the voters understood that football depends on many different things’ - he said.

‘I know I am not the kind of player who will dribble past 10 opponents before scoring a goal, but I can hurt teams in many different ways. You also have to know how to help the team clear corners, block shots or track back when the opponent breaks. [...] I see this Ballon d’Or as a reward for all those less spectacular aspects of the game, which I am very happy to perform.’

For Kane to be named the best in the world, however, it came down to the finest of margins. He finished just 28 points ahead of Mbappe, the smallest margin in the history of the Ballon d’Or. At 33, the England striker is reaching the peak of his career.

#1837. New Arsenal signing sends farewell message before completing 'landmark' transfer

Your weekly briefing on Arsenal, featuring team news and expert analysis from Matt Verri

Victor Ozhianvuna has bid an emotional farewell to Shamrock Rovers ahead of his move to Arsenal.

The highly-rated midfielder will head to north London after turning 18 in January, following a deal that was first agreed in October 2025.

Ozhianvuna is viewed as one of the brightest young talents in Irish football and has already made 37 senior appearances for reigning League of Ireland Premier Division champions Shamrock Rovers.

He also became the second-youngest player ever to feature in the UEFA Conference League last year.

His performances quickly caught the attention of Arsenal, who will add the Republic of Ireland Under-17 international to their academy ranks in the New Year.

Ozhianvuna - a boyhood Arsenal fan - has now said goodbye to Shamrock Rovers, where he has been since the age of six, penning a heartfelt statement on social media.

That was after a special presentation that recently took place with Ronan Finn, Shamrock Rovers’ director of football, plus their youth coach, Tony Cousins.

“After 11 amazing years, I’m saying goodbye to the club where I’ve made memories that I’ll never forget,” Ozhianvuna wrote on Instagram.

“I’ve met a lot of amazing people at the club and I’ve learned so much over the years as a footballer, but more importantly as a person and for that I’m forever grateful.

“I’d like to thank my coaches, my teammates and my friends and family for all the help over the years. I’d also like to thank the supporters for the constant love and support they’ve shown to me and to the club.

“The last few months have been difficult with an injury and I’m gutted to have not been able to play, but I couldn’t have asked for a better way to sign off than winning the league and lifting the trophy in front of the fans.

“As I move on to the next stage in my career, I’ll never forget the club that gave me a chance and I’m proud to say I’ve played for The Hoops. Forever grateful, Forever a Hoop.”
